annotated.instruct: Defensive and exasperated, with a sharp, clipped delivery.

annotated.text: Ruijerd was resolved in the destruction of the village, but then you showed up and I got impatient.

annotated.text: And because you didn’t look particularly vigilant, I thought I could take care of you easily.

annotated.text: I didn’t think that a plan to take care of me had been prepared......I could not have predicted a trap to hunt me down.....

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It wasn’t a trap.

Somehow, I’m sorry.

But Orsted or Randolph might have predicted such a situation.

Although I wish Orsted would tell me about these things in advance.......

No, now that I think about it, he did say to take the ring.

That might be why he kept quiet about it.

By simply wearing the ring, it renders the Dark King powerless, that sort of thing.

Words without worth.

Well, this wouldn’t be the first time Orsted has left out important information.

This also isn’t the first time I didn’t need to hear important information.
annotated.instruct: Narrator delivers the text in a calm, reflective tone, recounting events with a sense of irony and resignation.

annotated.text: ......Well there is the saying that overconfidence leads to defeat.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a resigned and bitter tone, acknowledging her own overconfidence.

annotated.text: Yes, truly.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat responds with a short, subdued affirmation, showing he understands the weight of Vita's words.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As Vita regretfully says that, he shrinks.

It’s as if he’s rapidly losing power.

And at the same time, the skeleton also begins to collapse.
annotated.instruct: Narrator describes the scene with a tone of dramatic tension, emphasizing Vita's physical and symbolic decline.

annotated.text: To think that I, the history’s strongest king of the Glutinous race, will be finished off in a place like this and in this way, I had never even dreamt of that. Rudeus of theQuagmire. Splendid work.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a mix of pride and despair, reflecting on her legacy and defeat.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
.....I wonder how I’ll get back.

I hadn’t predicted these turns of events.

Luck, I wonder if I can chalk it up to that.

I went to see Randolph myself, so I wouldn’t call that luck.

Then, would it be better if I told him not to call himself the history’s strongest?

No, there’s still something left that I need to hear from him.
annotated.instruct: Narrator reflects with a tone of introspection, contemplating the events and his own role in them.

annotated.text: There’s one thing I want to hear. Are you an apostle of Hitogami?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat asks with a tone of curiosity and urgency, seeking clarity about Vita's beliefs.

annotated.text: That’s right. I am greatly indebted to that God.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of reverence and gratitude, expressing her deep connection to Hitogami.

annotated.text: He set me free from the demonic hands of Death God Laxus and told me about the route to the Heaven Continent’s Hell.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of solemn reflection, recounting her past and the impact of Hitogami's intervention.

annotated.text: Thanks to him I have lived a long time......
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of weary acceptance, acknowledging the consequences of her long life.

annotated.text: And this is the result that came of that.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of philosophical contemplation, pondering the nature of her fate.

annotated.text: Is it cause and effect, or fate?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat asks with a tone of deep curiosity and existential questioning.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Vita continued to shrink rapidly.

When I first entered the room, he was as big as an average human, but now he’s no bigger than a fist.
annotated.instruct: Narrator describes the scene with a tone of dramatic urgency, emphasizing Vita's rapid transformation.

annotated.text: Rudeus, let me say one last thing.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of finality and emotional weight, preparing to deliver her last words.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: The Human God is a bad God, but there are those, although few in number, like me that he saved.
annotated.speaker: VITA
annotated.instruct: Vita speaks with a tone of conflicted reverence and bitterness, reflecting on Hitogami's role in her life.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As he said that, he had shrunk to the size of a fingertip.

At the same time, the skeleton was disappearing into sand.
annotated.instruct: Narrator describes the scene with a tone of eerie finality, emphasizing Vita's physical and symbolic dissolution.

annotated.text: Wait! Tell me who the other apostles might be........!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a tone of desperation and urgency, demanding answers.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
My consciousness also began to fade.

Part 5

I awoke.

My consciousness was clearing up.

I remember the contents of the dream and the last conversation in that room.
annotated.instruct: Narrator describes the scene with a tone of disorientation and confusion, reflecting on the aftermath of the encounter.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a tone of physical discomfort and confusion, reacting to the aftermath.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: There was an abrupt pain in my stomach followed by nausea.
annotated.instruct: Narrator describes the scene with a tone of visceral horror and shock, emphasizing the grotesque nature of the situation.

annotated.text: Blughgh......
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a tone of physical distress and confusion, reacting to the aftermath.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I dropped to all fours and the liquid was vomited out from my mouth.

A blue liquid.

A blue, slime-like substance, mixed with bile and dinner, spread on the ground.

Is it......the corpse of Dark King Vita?

As I thought that, a sense of discomfort began radiating from the ring on my left finger.

When I took my gauntlet off, the Death God’s ring broke and fell to the ground.

The ring sank into the vomit with a plop.
annotated.instruct: Narrator delivers the text with a tone of eerie silence and lingering unease, leaving the scene open-ended.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The fact that the ring is broken,

it means that the conversation with Vita earlier was real.

....Basically, Vita entered me and the ring caused him to self-destruct.

Pitiful.

That said, it wasn’t that Vita miscalculated.

If I had been manipulated, Hitogami’s victory would have been assured.

And I wouldn’t have been able to do a thing.....

A coincidence.

Or should I say inevitable.

The bone ring of the Death God Laxus.

It wasn’t just used to have Kishirika listen to its wearer.

It’s possible that Randolph didn’t even knew what it could really do.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of grim realization.

annotated.text: Aah, I wonder where Ruijerd went?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Curious and slightly anxious, as if searching for someone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I scan the surroundings.

I’m inside a building.

The floor, walls, and layout......all seem familiar.

It’s Ruijerd’s house.

From the turn of events, after Vita transferred to me, Ruijerd brought me here......?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of observation and mild confusion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It’s bright outside.

I wonder how many hours have passed.

It seems to already be dawn.

I’ll clean up the vomit later.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of tiredness and mild discomfort.

annotated.text: Ruijerd-san?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Curious and slightly concerned, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
There was no reply from the landlord.

Did he go outside?

Or is it something else?

For now, I stood up and started looking around.

I have to confirm the situation.

No, there he is.

Ruijerd was lying on the other side of the hearth.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of mild confusion and concern.

annotated.text: Ruije-
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Hesitant and slightly nervous, as if trying to call someone's name.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He was lying there, pale faced with wheezing breath.

Holding his own trembling body.

The moment I saw that, I was at a loss for words.

This was clearly not normal.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of shock and concern.

annotated.text: Vita was halting the progression of the disease. The moment Vita is killed, his fissions will die and the plague will spread again
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Determined and slightly urgent, as if explaining a critical situation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I remembered him saying that.

In other words, Ruijerd’s current state is.....
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of realization and concern.

annotated.text: The plague.....
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of realization and urgency.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It didn’t seem like the Dark King Vita had only died.

His self-destruction might have destroyed himself, but........

It was suicide bombing.

Chapter 244: Plague

Part 1

If Vita were to die, the progression of the plague will restart.

I was told in advance, but to think that it would be this extreme...

Perhaps Vita wasn’t delaying the progression of the disease, but had merely paralyzed it.

The paralysis was undone when he possessed me and then died, resulting in the disintegration of his fissions.

As a result, the symptoms surfaced all at once......or something like that.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of frustration and resignation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
‘I brought Vita down’, I’m not going to say that.

That was a suicide bombing.

I’m relieved that someone with the same level of stupidity was on Hitogami’s side, but I can’t be relieved about the present situation.
annotated.instruct: Surprised and slightly anxious, as if addressing someone urgently.

annotated.text: Rudeus-dono!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of urgency and confusion.

annotated.text: Sándor-san!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Concerned and slightly frantic, as if explaining a crisis.

annotated.text: Dark King Vita has fallen. The progress of the plague may have been affected as a result of that.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Determined and slightly urgent, as if explaining a critical situation.

annotated.text: Eh!? When? Where did you defeat the Dark King!?
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Angry and frustrated, as if reacting to bad news.

annotated.text: Just now, he selfishly chose defeat!
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of resignation and calm.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It’s fine either way.
annotated.instruct: Urgent and demanding, as if requesting a full explanation.

annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Urgent and demanding, as if requesting a full explanation.

annotated.text: Well......
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of determination and clarity.

I started explaining.

What I heard from Ruijerd last night.

How Vita was transferred to me through oral contact, how I was shown illusions, and how the Death God’s ring defeated him.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.text: ........I understand. In other words, the Dark King challenged you but the tables turned on him, and that.....Ruijerd-dono was just being manipulated, right?

annotated.text: ........I didn’t realize it until I woke up, but if he had been an enemy, he wouldn’t have carried me to the village.

annotated.text: Got it.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD

annotated.speaker: RUIJERD

annotated.text: For now, have whoever is mobile go and recover those who were out hunting.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD

annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Ruijerd speaks with a determined, organized tone, outlining next steps.

It hasn’t been very long since the spread of the disease, he’s excellent.

I turned my gaze to see Doga noisily running while carrying a woman in his arms.

And as if to chase him, the children of the Supard race were following him with concerned looks on their faces.

They’re probably headed towards.......the chieftain’s lecture hall.

It is the largest building here, so it’s perfect.

According to Doga, there are no deceased yet.

But more than half of the people, just like Ruijerd, are experiencing symptoms to the point of immobility.

annotated.text: Rudeus-dono, what should we do?

annotated.text: ......What to do.
annotated.speaker: SUPARD
annotated.instruct: Supard speaks with a hesitant, uncertain tone, showing confusion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I find myself at a loss for words being asked what to do.

This situation.

What must be done?

The village is being invaded by the plague.

We must do something to cure them.

Therefore, right, detoxification magic.

But I just tried it on Ruijerd.

Obviously, there wasn’t any effect.

It’s not that I was able to use every form of healing magic, but I feel as if the possibility of detoxification magic not having any effect is very high.

Since there are many such diseases and poisons.

If detoxification magic won’t work, then I should leave it to the disease specialist.

Although I say that, who fits that description?

Should I ask Ariel to make preparations for a doctor?

But the one who is the most knowledgeable about diseases is Orsted.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But Orsted, and the Supard race.....

No, let’s just try and ask him.

First of all, a means of communication.

Three days left until the establishment of the magic formation.....

No, I knew something like this would happen, so I had already prepared a teleportation magic formation in the basement of the office in advance.

Let’s install the Communication Lithograph and magic formation in this village as well.

I’ll teleport to the office and report to Orsted about the current situation.

I’ll also report to the branches, from the main office, the condition of the Supard race.

If all of that was useless......we’ll think about that when the time comes.

Alright.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.text: We should set up a teleportation magic formation in the village, move to the office, from there contact the branches, and thus call for someone capable of a medical examination.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a calm, decisive tone, outlining a plan.

annotated.text: Roger. Then I shall defend the village and nurse the patients.
annotated.speaker: SUPARD
annotated.instruct: Supard speaks with a resolute, determined tone, accepting responsibility.

annotated.text: Please do.
annotated.speaker: SUPARD
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
We quickly exchanged words, and then I hurried towards the end of the village.

Since we’re inside a deep forest, the concentration of magic is high.

A teleportation magic formation can be set up without the need of any magic crystals.

Just to be sure, I should bring what’s needed for the lithograph and set it up in the village.

While deeply thinking about that, I headed towards the other side of the village.

Exiting out of the fence, cutting down the trees with magic to make an open space, I then made a hut with earth magic.

A hut with no entrance.

I dug a tunnel from beneath the hut and connected it with the inside of village. With this, the monsters won’t come.

I took out my memo and verified the magic formula with compliance to the preliminaries of the magic formation.

Now to make sure that the drawing doesn’t vanish from the floor, I created a lithograph from magic and drew upon it.

Impatience is a taboo.

If I make the slightest mistake, the magic formation won’t be completed.

Rather than wasting time debugging, I want to make it work in one go if I can.

When you're in a hurry, that's when you should calm down.
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a frustrated, exasperated tone.

annotated.text: Ah, damn.....
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Or so I was thinking. I ended up making a small mistake.
annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a frustrated, exasperated tone.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Deep breaths.

Composing myself, I decided to draw it slower than I normally do.

A plain magic formation with a diameter of 2 meters.[26]

If I draw it hastily, I will make a mistake.

Carefully drawing.

I’ve drawn the teleportation magic formation myself many times over.

I should have the confidence to draw it accurately from the start.

With that in mind I calmed myself, and I carefully finished drawing the teleportation magic formation.
annotated.instruct: Supard speaks with a curious, concerned tone, seeking confirmation.

annotated.text: How is it?
annotated.speaker: SUPARD
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after each line for emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I pour my magic into it as soon as it was completed.

The entirety of the drawn magic formation is poured with my magic. On which it began emitting a dim light. It’s a success.
annotated.instruct: Unknown speaker speaks with a brief, affirming tone.

annotated.text: Alright.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I immediately jumped on it.

Part 2
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
After my consciousness disappeared for an instant, the basement of the office appeared in front of me. Normal operation of the magic formation was confirmed.

And at the same time, I set out for the door at a quick pace.

Not even abiding by the written message
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Those who have business with Orsted and Rudeus. This way.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Authoritative, commanding tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
, I go towards the upper levels.

I come out of the basement, which is adjacent to the teleportation magic formation room, and ascend the stairs to enter the lobby.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Ah, chairman, welcome ba----
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Hesitant, surprised tone.

annotated.text: Is the president here!?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Hesitant, surprised tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: To my threatening attitude, the receptionist twitched her ears. While lowering them, with a slightly frightened look, she gave an answer.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: H-he’s here.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Without hearing her words, I continued towards the president’s office and opened the door before she’s finished.

I passed through the corridor, which was rather short, and opened the door to his office.

I thought of myself as not that rude, but I forgot to knock.

As a result, I saw Orsted without his helmet on.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Orsted-sama.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted was showing a seemingly awkward-ish face,

But he didn’t hide it and was looking straight at me.

When I stared at it for several seconds, it seemed like he was saying ‘Do you have any problems?’, to which I felt my anger swell up.

I know that this was not the time to get angry.

Still, the words that came out of my mouth were demanding, distracted by my irritation.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Say, the Supard Race’s illness, were you aware of it?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: I was aware of it.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: And a way to cure it?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: There is none.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I was told bluntly.

It wasn’t that he didn’t know but there was none.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: If you had told me sooner, I should have been able to at least search for a cure. Why didn’t you tell me about it sooner?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: As I said that, Orsted shook his head.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: When you became my subordinate, the Supard race was supposed to have already perished.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Supposed.....are you talking about if it were the usual loops?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: That’s right. And Ruijerd Supardia never even got to meet the surviving Supard race.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
They were supposed to have already perished, that’s why he didn’t say anything.

Ruijerd was normally unrelated to that event.

Since he was reminded of that as a possibility, he didn’t say anything, is that how it is?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: But you visited them a few years back, correct?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Delivered with a tone of reluctant admission and hesitation.

annotated.text: At that time, you found the Supard race, got in contact with Ruijerd, confirmed that a plague was spreading and yet, you kept quiet?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a mix of accusation and disbelief, rising in intensity.

annotated.text: That’s right.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Flat and resigned, as if confirming a grim truth.

annotated.text: If you had kept quiet then the Supard race would perish and Ruijerd too would disappear. Since I wouldn’t know, you gave up, is that what you thought!
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Voice rises sharply with anger and betrayal, full of emotional weight.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Before I realized it, I was shouting.

I felt like I was betrayed.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.text: Wrong. I thought it was a waste of time.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Said with a tone of confusion and mild disbelief.

annotated.text: A waste of......time?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Delivered with a hesitant, questioning tone.

annotated.text: That’s right. Even I tried to save the Supards.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of determination and resolve.

annotated.text: I tried every detoxification magic, gave them medicine that would likely cure them, I tried everything.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Voice carries frustration and a sense of futility.

annotated.text: But they weren’t cured. That plague can’t be cured.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of resignation and grim acceptance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: So Orsted tried everything that he could think of?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.text: The ruin of the Supards was a pre-determined fact for me. But you wouldn’t give up if you knew, and would possibly look after them until their ruin.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Delivered with a tone of reluctant agreement and resignation.

annotated.text: That is.....of course.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of hesitation and uncertainty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But, two years ago.....or even before then?

As for the timing, possibly after that one assignment in Shirone Kingdom, unaware of the location of Laplace’s rebirth, I proposed assembling war potential.

At that time, if I had been told about the Supards, I would have been running around thinking of how to tackle the situation.

At least, I wouldn’t have been able to do all the work this past year.

I wouldn’t have been able to call out to Atofe, Randolf, and the rest of the demon kings.

Or perhaps I wouldn’t have even gone to Milis.

It’s also possible that I would be unaware of Gisu being an apostle.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.text: But, deciding whether it’s a waste of time is....I....then, no.....it might be.....
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of confusion and uncertainty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I understand the reason.

But my heart can’t catch up yet.

A good excuse doesn’t come to mind.

This time, Orsted hadn’t forgotten.

He just didn’t say it.

He intentionally schemed so to not let me help the Supard race.

Even though I understand the reason, I cannot, at any cost, forgive him.

Orsted tried to let my benefactor die without any help.

Orsted is like that, so it can’t be helped.

Even though such words come forth normally.

I can’t forgive him.

Not good.

At this rate, I'll think of Orsted as an enemy.

In the midst of such an operation.

With the enemy in Biheiril Kingdom, while everyone’s there......

An excuse, I must think of an excuse.....an excuse to forgive Orsted.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.text: ........Is Ruijerd a hindrance to your plans?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Delivered with a tone of confusion and mild disbelief.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Those were the words that came out.

Words that don’t go with the flow of conversation.

If this was to be true, then what would I intend to do?

But Orsted said this.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.text: He’s not a hindrance. His daughter, who is going to fight Laplace, is the most important piece.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of confusion and curiosity.

annotated.text: His daughter? How is she important?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Delivered with a tone of confusion and mild disbelief.

annotated.text: Laplace, who has become a Demon God, is immortal. But he has a weak point. The Supards, with their third eye, are the only ones who can see it and deal the fatal blow.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The only ones who can take advantage of the Demon God’s weak point are the Supards.
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of realization and shock.

annotated.text: Ah.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Then, something suddenly struck me.

The reason why Laplace transferred his curse to the Supards to destroy them.

The reason why Ruijerd, who inferior in fighting strength against Laplace, was able to put a blow on him during the fight of the three demon slaying heroes; to the point where even Perugius expresses his gratitude.

The reason why the Supard race was struck with the plague.

The reason why the plague was slower than expected, but progressed after Ruijerd’s arrival.

.....The reason I travelled together with Ruijerd to the Central Continent.
annotated.instruct: Spoken with a tone of realization and shock.

annotated.text: So.....it’s Hitogami.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration, with a slight pause before the next line.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Strength leaves my body.

Unsteady on my feet, I step back.

Something caught my foot and I sat in a chair.
annotated.instruct: Speak with a trembling voice, showing physical weakness and instability.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Putting my weight on the armrest, the chair stopped sliding.
annotated.instruct: Deliver with a calm, steady tone, emphasizing the chair's sudden stop.

annotated.text: In the original history, Ruijerd-san survived, correct?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with a curious and slightly hesitant tone, showing uncertainty.

annotated.text: Yes.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Answer with a short, firm tone, conveying certainty.

annotated.text: Since he didn’t die on the way, he created a child at the end, correct?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with a slightly more intense tone, showing growing curiosity.

annotated.text: Yes.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Confident and assertive, with a slight edge of authority.

annotated.text: Orsted-sama, you would make use of that child to defeat Laplace, correct?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm, measured tone, revealing a shift in strategy.

annotated.text: In the beginning, yes. After I learned that Laplace is mortal the moment he’s born, I didn’t use her or anything.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Deliver with a reflective, slightly regretful tone, showing past decisions.

annotated.text: Is that so.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Say with a dry, almost dismissive tone, showing realization.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Then, this is also one of Hitogami’s plans.

I see.

And now, this time he coordinated in order to erase me......huh.

Aiming to kill two birds with one stone, a strategy most befitting of Hitogami.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a contemplative tone, highlighting the weight of the revelation.

annotated.text: Orsted-sama. Looks like we’re being manipulated at the hands of Hitogami again.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a concerned and slightly accusatory tone, showing frustration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: The ruin of the Supards, the rampancy of the plague isn’t a natural phenomenon, it’s Hitogami’s work. Looks like it’s convenient for Hitogami as long as Demon God Laplace is alive.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: State with a calm but firm tone, revealing a shocking truth.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Rather than the Demon Dragon King, Laplace who became the Demon God is no harm to him.

Since he has forgotten about Hitogami anyway.

On the contrary, he’s destroying the humans.

Unexpectedly, it’s possible that during Laplace’s military campaign, he himself was being manipulated by Hitogami.

I don’t think he could manipulate the dragon race directly, possibly through an apostle.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, thoughtful tone, reflecting on complex events.

annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Exhale with a heavy, weary tone, showing emotional exhaustion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I somehow felt refreshed because of this unexpected result.

Orsted didn’t talk about the Supards. Well, that’s still lurking in the back of my mind though.

Even if I direct my anger towards Orsted here, there won’t be any agreement anyway.

It will only delight Hitogami.

He’ll just laugh with a broad grin while saying ‘Just as planned.’[27]
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slightly refreshed and reflective tone, showing a shift in perspective.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It didn’t occur to me before, but I thought up of a good excuse as a result of feeling refreshed.

Unaware of a method to cure the plague, thinking that they were already doomed, Orsted neglected them.

Before, he thought that the ruin of the Supard race was not related to the life and death of Ruijerd.

He may also be thinking of Ruijerd’s whereabouts.

But then he thought ‘perhaps’ and went to see it for himself, only to find Ruijerd there.

Moreover, Ruijerd had gotten infected as well.

He didn’t know how to tell me about this, perhaps it might even be better to not tell me. He couldn’t help but think that.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, introspective tone, revealing internal thoughts.

annotated.text: How did you intended to defeat Laplace without the Supards?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with a direct and probing tone, showing determination.

annotated.text: Using the Godsword is not that absurd of a choice. I can’t avoid a hard fight, but you’re currently assembling comrades, so we’ll somehow pull through.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Answer with a confident and resolute tone, showing determination.

annotated.text: But if I recall correctly, that Godsword? Using it takes a lot of mana, doesn’t it?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with a skeptical and questioning tone, showing doubt.

annotated.text: You can’t substitute your back for your belly.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: State with a firm and slightly admonishing tone, showing wisdom.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
[28]

On top of that, Orsted intended to take responsibility as a penalty.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a heavy, regretful tone, showing remorse.

annotated.text: I thought about apologizing to you. But I couldn’t speak, and now it took this shape. It was inexcusable.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Speak with a sincere and apologetic tone, showing humility.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Orsted said that and bowed his head in apology.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, accepting tone, showing understanding.

annotated.text: .....I understand.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of regret and humility.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted isn’t perfect.

These things may also happen.

Let’s just forgive him with a big heart.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a warm, forgiving tone.

annotated.text: Orsted-sama, I’ll forgive you only for this time.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a respectful and slightly hesitant tone.

annotated.text: Yes.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Respond with a short, firm affirmation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
With this, it’s settled.

All~right, let’s face forward.

That is, for now.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, forward-looking tone.

annotated.text: I’m just making sure, but you do need mana to defeat Hitogami, yes?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a concerned and inquisitive tone.

annotated.text: Yes.
annotated.speaker: SUPARD
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm, resolute tone, conveying quiet determination and a sense of duty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Hitogami prevented the specific place in the Shirone Kingdom where Laplace would revive.

Moreover, he tried to exterminate the Supard race’s last survivor by letting Ruijerd find the Supard village; Ruijerd who is the key to defeating Laplace.

If the entire Supard race is exterminated, then Laplace can be thrown at Orsted.

Orsted, in order to defeat Laplace, will have to use a large amount of mana.

This should be the winning move for Hitogami.

We’ll crush that winning move.

We better not use the Godsword then.

Avoiding fights as much as possible, and minimizing mana consumption as well.

I will assemble the war potential in order to bring down Laplace, making Orsted’s mana explode during the fight with Hitogami.

But for that purpose, the Supard race, who are a key point in defeating Laplace, must be kept alive.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a detailed, strategic tone.

annotated.text: I’ve heard it already, but there isn’t any method to cure them, right?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of uncertainty and hesitation.

annotated.text: ...........At the very least, I have no knowledge.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Respond with a tone of quiet resignation.

annotated.text: Although you say that, there are things even you don’t know of, eh?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a slightly teasing and confident tone.

annotated.text: That’s.....right.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Respond with a tone of reluctant agreement.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted said that and wore his frightening face as usual.

I’ve grown accustomed to that angry look these days.

This is the face when he’s ashamed.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a determined and hopeful tone.

annotated.text: Then perhaps there just might be a method. Let’s struggle for a bit more.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a resolute and encouraging tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Even Orsted might not have been able to try many methods, because of his curse.

He should’ve been able to do something, but couldn’t because of the current state of his curse.

Then, we should try and do it.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of cautious optimism.

annotated.text: Got it......I’ll head towards the village as well.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Respond with a firm, decisive tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted said that and nodded.

Part 3

We came back to the village after three hours.

During that time, I reported about my encounter with Dark King Vita.

I explained Vita’s suicide bombing by the Death God’s ring, to which Orsted hid his surprised face by instead showing an angry look.

By looking at his face, it seemed he didn't know about Vita’s possessing power.

Maybe it was truly a great insurance.

After that, we used the Communication Lithograph and contacted the branches.

About the nature of the disease of the Supard race, and arrangements for a doctor.

The number of C.L was too high, so it took time contacting every branch by transmission.

The functionality of a carbon copy is necessary.

While I was waiting for the reply to my message, I drew the preliminary sketch of an additional teleportation magic circle.

To set up a teleportation magic circle, you first have to draw two. After confirming the activation, you erase wherever you had written the other down. There is a need to go through this process.

There is no need to charge it now, but when it is used, it has to be charged thoroughly.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a detailed, informative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The receptionist’s job was to stand by at the office; during Orsted’s absence, she would answer the mail and guide anyone who comes through the teleportation magic circle.

These days, the teleportation magic circles have grown so much that it’s becoming difficult to remember which is connected to which. A guide map may be necessary for first time guests rather than me and Orsted.

I should also write down where to move in the forest after getting teleported.

By the way, Sylphy had already left to the Holy Land of Swords with Ghyslaine and Izolte.

During that time, Ariel visited as well and had a talk with Sylphy.

The receptionist and Orsted didn’t hear any details, but there wasn’t a message left, which meant that she just came to visit for a while.

Because I had that kind of dream, I may become a little self-conscious if I met her.

I don’t want to blush in front of Sylphy while looking at Ariel.

After that, the establishment of the teleportation magic circle and communication lithograph by everyone else who went to Biheiril Kingdom had been confirmed.

Everything was operating favourably.

It looks like the others are doing well too.

I contacted them as well.

There’s no problem with Aisha+Mercenary group.

Zanoba reported about a subjugation force being assembled in the capital city.

Roxy reported about investigating the whereabouts of Ogre God.

I sent them messages regarding the present situation.

At the end, I added
annotated.instruct: Speak with a commanding and reassuring tone.

annotated.text: We’ll somehow manage over here, so please carry on with your respective duties.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of mild concern and expectation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
If I don’t, I can expect Eris flying to me.

Then, there were a lot of favourable replies from many countries.

A lot of countries gave the reply
annotated.instruct: Speak with a determined and focused tone.

annotated.text: We’ll investigate about the disease from past documents.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of cautious relief and anticipation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Asura Kingdom was ready to send over a doctor by tomorrow.

The only reply that’s left is the one from Milis, regarding reinforcements.

Sending in the Temple Knight Party via teleportation magic circle is rather difficult, so it’s discouraged.

At any rate, the reply from Milis is late nonetheless.

Anyhow, after doing all of that, I came back to the village.

Together with Orsted.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of quiet observation and reflection.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted is currently looking at the fallen Supards one by one.

He probably has better medical knowledge than the average doctor, but he still couldn’t understand the cause for the disease, so it’s not like he would understand it at this stage.

In the first place, he’s not a doctor.

He may have tried to cure some diseases in the previous loops, but never had actually medically treated someone.

If pushed, I’d say it’s like a RPG errand event.[29]

On X day of X month, Rudeus becomes sick.

Rudeus, on X day of X month will die, so we must cure him before then.

At this point, you do not know the cure.

However, before that time comes, we come to know that Sylphiette-chan is experiencing the same disease.

And then Sylphiette-chan has an item used on her by Roxy and the disease is cured.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of analytical reflection and comparison.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted uses the item used by Roxy on Rudeus on the next turn.

That kind of feeling.

Well, by reconciling the past cases and the present cases we can look for a cure, that kind of diagnosis is possible, but I’m not a doctor so I wouldn’t know.

In short, Orsted isn’t too potent regarding affairs that are beyond expectations.
annotated.instruct: Respond with a tone of quiet frustration and uncertainty.

annotated.text: I still don’t know.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Deliver with uncertainty and hesitation, voice slightly strained.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: After examining everyone, feeling powerless, he shook his head.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of helplessness and resignation.

annotated.text: I feel like the symptoms differ a little from the plague I know of......
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Speak with mild concern and confusion, voice slightly uncertain.

annotated.text: Differ, in what way?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with curiosity and a slight edge of impatience.

annotated.text: The deterioration wasn’t supposed to be this rapid.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: State with growing concern and a hint of frustration.

annotated.text: ......So Vita was paralyzing it after all, I wonder if that’s the only thing that came to light.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Mutter with contemplation and a touch of uncertainty.

annotated.text: If it’s Hitogami’s way of doing things, then it’s possible.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with cautious optimism and a hint of realization.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Pretending to suppress the disease, but in reality he didn’t do anything.

It’s Hitogami’s way of doing things.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of resignation and understanding.

annotated.text: Do you have something on your end?
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Ask with a tone of genuine inquiry and slight hesitation.

annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Respond with a tone of quiet defeat and resignation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
While Orsted was examining the illness, I was listening to the people helping out with the medical treatment how they used a remedy when the disease first struck.

They collected some popular herbs from the Central Continent or vegetables with high nutritional values and cooked them together to make a mash of it and gave it to the affected.

I’m not that knowledgeable about the nutritional value of vegetables or herbs, but I can’t think of it as a big mistake.

This is a dead end.

We must change our way of thinking.

For example.......right.

Originally the spread of the plague was supposed to be faster.

Which means, Hitogami can control this plague. Then, some kind of poison was brought in from somewhere, so that possibility also exists?

Or perhaps the timing when the Supards were struck with the plague simply deviated because of the teleport incident.

Hitogami can simply use that and be able to.......

Ah jeez, just which is it?

The thing that is important right now is finding a cure for this disease, not Hitogami.

The more I think about it, the more I feel my thoughts sinking into a quagmire.

I somehow felt that perhaps, there might not even be a method.

An unpleasant premonition.

But, not yet.

At least, Orsted and I, together with Sándor and Doga, can’t come up with anything.

But after this, a doctor is coming.

Let’s just concentrate on maintaining the patient’s hygiene and providing them with nutrition.

While thinking that, I spent the whole day nursing with Sándor and Doga.

Part 4

The next day, a team of doctors from the Asura Kingdom arrived.

Two doctors and four nurses along with numerous food and medical supplies.

For the time being, it looks like they’re all people who don’t fear the Supard race.

After looking at the patients, they immediately started their medical examination.

Whether or not they would disclose info about the teleportation magic circle, I have no choice but to rely on Ariel’s charisma.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of deep frustration and determination.

annotated.text: We were told in advance about it, but we’ve never seen these types of symptoms.
annotated.speaker: Ariel
annotated.instruct: Speak with professional concern and a hint of confusion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Not to mention, we took such a risk and yet the team of doctors were useless.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of disappointment and resignation.

annotated.text: We have performed medical examinations of demon race in the domestic, but......if we’re to handle a specific demon race under specific circumstances, then there’s nothing we can do.
annotated.speaker: Ariel
annotated.instruct: Speak with professional caution and a hint of helplessness.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I don’t get it at all.

Those are the opinions of the doctors.

At least, it doesn’t come under the category of past cases.

That’s understood, since the human doctors have seen them and Orsted as well.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of reluctant acceptance and resignation.

annotated.text: We will continue the examination just in case, but it would be better to not expect too much.
annotated.speaker: Ariel
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of cautious optimism and professional restraint.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The doctor said that and went back to treat the patients.

But.....even so, I see.

I hadn't expected much, but to be told that clearly... My disappointment was greater than I thought.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of deep sorrow and emotional weight.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of quiet despair and emotional strain.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
While breathing a sigh, I survey the surroundings.

There, a great number of Supards were arranged in a line.

The ones who are moaning, ones who are dead tired and aren’t moving, ones who are sleeping.

The ones who are lying down being nursed, a scene just like a field hospital.

There aren’t any deceased yet, but there are many with severe symptoms.

And Ruijerd is also included among those with severe symptoms.

Currently, he has lost consciousness and is in a comatose state.

At times, he suddenly opens his eyes and starts coughing violently. By looking at him, I understand that he doesn't have much time.

I want to cure him somehow.

I think as I sit near Ruijerd.

But, we don’t have anything to go with and no breakthrough solution comes to mind.

Only the time is passing by.

With this, even if doctors came from the Milis and Kingdom of the Dragon King, the possibility of finding a cure is low.

If we couldn’t find a cure, what should be done next?

Whom should I ask, would that person understand?

What should be done.....?

What can I do?
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of somber observation and emotional weight.

annotated.text: Rudeus-dono.
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of respectful urgency and concern.
