annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a sense of shock and urgency.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I was hit by the golden armor.

One hit.

With just one hit, my armor was completely broken into pieces, and I took flight with my hazy consciousness.

My consciousness was receding.

As I was about to fall unconscious, I saw it.

Eris, Ruijerd, Atofe, and Malta.

Attacking the Fighting God all at once.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a somber and reflective tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
───────That day, Third City Heilelul was annihilated.

Part 3

When I came to, I could smell something nice.

I could smell a little bit of sweat too, but it was nice.

A nice smell that I was accustomed to.

I could see red hair swaying at the edge of my vision.

At the same time, I could feel warmth around my cheeks.

My cheeks were touching something.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and curious tone.

annotated.text: ........Are you awake now?
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Soft, gentle, and caring voice.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
A voice came out from that something that was touching my cheeks.

It was Eris’s voice.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a sudden jolt of awareness.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
And then my consciousness quickly came back.

Eris was carrying me on her shoulders.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a sense of clarity and urgency.

annotated.text: ........What’s going on?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Confused, hesitant, and nervous tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I quickly stood up and surveyed my surroundings.

Many people were walking around the surroundings like refugees.

Cliff, Elinalize, and Ruijerd.
annotated.instruct: Defeated, resigned, and weary tone.

annotated.text: We lost.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a somber and reflective tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
After that, Eris and the others challenged the Fighting God, and were completely defeated.

Eris fainted in just one hit, and Elinalize’s shield broke.

Malta and Atofe put up a good fight, but they were still sent flying every time.

Moore took over when I fainted and told everyone to retreat.

Ruijerd collected Eris and I. And then with Atofe, the Imperial Guards, Malta, and Sándor who regained consciousness as the rear guard, the retreat was successful.
annotated.instruct: Resigned, defeated, and weary tone.

annotated.text: I see.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a sense of realization and regret.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It was a shock.

It was a shock that we were so easily defeated.

I never really thought of myself as the strongest.

Even when I fought for the first time with the MK. I, I lost to Orsted.

It wasn’t invincible.

But I was certainly getting victorious these days.

I defeated both Atofe and Alek.

Regarding Alek, it wasn’t a solo battle, but a victory was still a victory.

But I should’ve always taken the assumption that I would lose.

But one punch was a first for me

It was one hit.

With just one hit, my armor broke into pieces and I fell unconscious.

.......I might’ve underestimated Badigadi.

Was it because I thought that even if he was the Fighting God, he would still cut corners being that Demon Lord-sama?
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of reflection and regret, emphasizing the shock of defeat.

annotated.text: What are we supposed to do next?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with uncertainty and a questioning tone, showing hesitation and seeking guidance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
On Eris’s inquiry, I pondered.

Next.

What should be done next?

We hadn’t run out of options.

But I wonder if we can win against that Fighting God with my impertinent plan.

We didn’t have Sándor nor Atofe, nor the Imperial Guards.

They might’ve died as well.

Our fighting force was uncertain.

There was Eris, Ruijerd, Cliff, Elinalize, and me........and then some warriors of the Supard race.

Even if I say that, I couldn’t be counted as a war potential. I, who had lost the MK. I, was only an insect now.

The best I could do right now was to make rivers, make mountains, and set fire to the mountains.

The Three Charms.[44]

The Fighting God would just drink up the river, jump over the mountains, and extinguish the fire on the mountains with the water that he drank and then come after us.

We couldn’t win with our current potential.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a contemplative and analytical tone, weighing options and expressing doubt.

annotated.text: There’s no way but to run.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Speak with a firm and resigned tone, suggesting the only viable option is to flee.

annotated.text: ......Ruijerd-san.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a hesitant and respectful tone, addressing Ruijerd with concern.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Ruijerd spoke while looking at me.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm and factual tone, describing Ruijerd's actions and demeanor.

annotated.text: That guy is one of the Seven Great World Powers, the real deal. He’s not someone who can be defeated even if we attacked him in a group.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Speak with a grave and authoritative tone, emphasizing the overwhelming power of the enemy.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
So we should run.

We should run until the Supard village........

And then.......what?

If it were the Three Charms, then the priest-sama that took shelter in the temple used his wit to exterminate the mountain witch.

Orsted(The Priest) was there in the Supard village.

But.......Fighting God Badigadi and Gisu.

Their aim was my life, and to exhaust Orsted’s mana.

And if Orsted were to fight the Fighting God, his mana consumption would be nowhere near the level that it would have been if he had fought the Sword God or North God.

It was a substantial defeat.

To achieve their goals, they would go to the ends of the world.

No matter where we go, there won’t be a place safe for us.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of despair and realization, highlighting the futility of running.

annotated.text: .......Even if we run, we can’t win.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a determined and resolute tone, suggesting a final stand despite inevitable defeat.

annotated.text: Then there’s no choice but to fight with the resolution of an honorable defeat.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a somber and resigned tone, acknowledging the inevitability of death.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
A fight with a resolution of an honorable defeat would still be a defeat.

We couldn’t win.

If we died, it would be over.
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm and commanding tone, urging Rudeus to regain composure.

annotated.text: ........Rudeus, get a hold of yourself.
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a warm and reassuring tone, emphasizing Eris's support and past connection.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Eris suddenly held my hand.

It was a strong and warm hand.

It was a hand which had saved me many times.

It was the hand which had held my child.
annotated.instruct: Speak with a startled and emotional tone, reacting to Eris's gesture.

annotated.text: Ah.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a focused and determined tone, shifting from despair to seeking a solution.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I calmed down a bit.

Think.

Think about a way to win.

First, there’s a need for information.

For example, the weakness of the Fighting God Armor.

But I heard that the Fighting God Armor was the best armor made by Laplace himself.

Even the person who built it himself was tied in his battle.

Would there even be a weakness?

But even if there wasn’t any weakness, there might be some kind of capture method. There was still a way to fight.

And from there, we could probably find some kind of hint.

Who is the one who knows that?

Atofe is.......not here.

Orsted?

That’s right, I must ask him.

And if we still couldn’t get anything........
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a contemplative and urgent tone, emphasizing the need for information and action.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
No.

Even if we couldn’t get anything, he was an enemy that we must fight someday.

We will fight now.

Atofe, Malta, and Sándor weren’t here.

But there should be a method to win.

But still, I want to keep the damage to a bare minimum.

I didn’t want to involve the Supard village with the battle.

Since Norn was there as well.

There should be a chance.

Even if it was less than 1%.

That’s right.

Now that I think about it, I still had one trump card left.

I originally planned to use that trump card much sooner.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a resolute and strategic tone, outlining a plan despite uncertainty.

annotated.text: .........We’ll retreat until the village and hold out there.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Speak with a firm and practical tone, suggesting a tactical retreat to the village.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I decided to wager on that.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a decisive and confident tone, confirming the plan to proceed.

annotated.text: Got it.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm and resolute tone, acknowledging the plan and moving forward.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Everybody nodded.

Part 4

Then, we returned back to the Supard village.

My trump card was still being prepared.

I wonder just what was really going on.

Would it be fine to just wait?

While suppressing my wavering heart, I sat in front of Orsted in seiza and reported to him everything that had happened up until yesterday.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a somber and factual tone, summarizing the situation and missing allies.

annotated.text: That’s all. We don’t know what has become of Sándor, Atofe, and Malta.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tense and expectant tone, setting the stage for Orsted's reaction.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Orsted wore a rigid expression.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tense and serious tone, describing Orsted's expression and the gravity of the moment.

annotated.text: Fighting God Badigadi?
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Speak with a cold and intimidating tone, emphasizing the threat posed by Fighting God Badigadi.

annotated.text: Do you know of any capture method?
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Speak with a commanding and intense tone, showing authority.

annotated.text: .......No. I know about the Fighting God Armor, but I’ve never once fought Badigadi wearing the Fighting God Armor.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a slow, deliberate pace, emphasizing the contrast between knowledge and experience.

annotated.text: I see.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Say the line in a neutral, monotone voice, expressing mild disappointment.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I had expected this, but I still couldn’t hide my disappointment.

But there was no need to show it on the surface.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, reflective tone, conveying subtle disappointment.

annotated.text: Then, please tell me about the Fighting God Armor.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a curious and inquisitive tone, showing interest in the topic.

annotated.text: Fighting God Armor is the best armor made by Laplace himself.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a factual and informative tone, emphasizing the armor's origin.

annotated.text: It sank to the innermost part of the Magical Cavern, at the center of the Rings Sea.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm, informative tone, highlighting the armor's unique properties.

annotated.text: Its surface gives out a golden spark when fired with mana, bestowing its user with the strongest power possible. But that much mana makes it sentient, and it hijacks the user’s mind.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a questioning and slightly concerned tone.

annotated.text: But, it didn’t seem like Badigadi’s mind was hijacked?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, analytical tone, expressing uncertainty and observation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
At the very least, I didn’t feel like Badigadi was being manipulated.

It was the same Badigadi as in my memories.

Although, it was possible that he was being manipulated, but it wasn't apparent.

After all, he didn’t bother arguing with Atofe and Sandor.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a contemplative tone, reflecting on the implications of the statement.

annotated.text: ......It will take some time before a complete hijack.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, explaining the armor's effects and Badigadi's unique traits.

annotated.text: From the moment one puts it on, the Fighting God Armor will start dominating your mind, and you will gradually be unable to differentiate between good and evil, and will only wish to fight. Although, Badigadi’s body is made up of a special meat which can’t be perceived by the Demon Eye. It’s possible that the Fighting God Armor can’t completely take over him.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a thoughtful and slightly puzzled tone, reflecting on the information provided.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
So that meant Badigadi hadn’t worn it for that long.

Still, I’ve heard about this hijack thing somewhere before........
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, informative tone, comparing the armor to other types of armor.

annotated.text: The Fighting God Armor is similar to your Magic Armor. The only difference it has from yours, which moves with the wearer’s mana as fuel, is that it takes the wearer’s very life force as a fuel and you can’t take it off until it completely drains you of it.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, emphasizing the armor's endurance.

annotated.text: If it has attached itself to Badigadi’s body, it can almost operate forever.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, explaining the armor's adaptability.

annotated.text: The moment that the armor is put on, it will adjust itself to the perfect shape for the wearer. In doing so, the optimal weapon is obtained.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, discussing the armor's combat range.

annotated.text: Although the weapon range depends on the weapon itself, if Badigadi equips it, it probably won't be long distance.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, explaining the armor's magical resistance.

annotated.text: The golden light radiating from the armor will render most magic ineffective.......but there is a limit. Your full powered stone cannon may be able to get through.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, reflective tone, acknowledging the speaker's knowledge and suggesting an alternative approach.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He’s very knowledgeable.

But I see, rather than a lightning strike, the stone cannon would have been more effective.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, inquisitive tone, addressing the speaker with respect.

annotated.text: Orsted-sama, when you fought the Fighting God, who was wearing the armor?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, factual tone, providing information about the previous wearer.

annotated.text: One of the Sea race. Although, his mana quickly ran out and he died.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, inquisitive tone, seeking further information.

annotated.text: Any other cases?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, informative tone, listing different wearers of the armor.

annotated.text: I’ve put it on myself a few times, a human put it on once, and a Demon race once.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, reflective tone, expressing curiosity about the speaker's experience.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He experienced it himself before?

Well, I guess if he hadn’t put it on himself a few times, he wouldn't have understood the details.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, inquisitive tone, seeking a solution to the problem.

annotated.text: So how exactly are we supposed to defeat it?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a calm, hesitant tone, expressing uncertainty.

annotated.text: ......I do not know.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak in a hesitant, uncertain tone, as if unsure of the answer.

annotated.text: You don't know?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Voice is sharp and questioning, with a slight edge of disbelief.

annotated.text: When wearing the Fighting God Armor, you feel neither pain nor fatigue. And on top of that, it is possible to fight constantly at full strength. But it is simply forcing you to move. It cannot heal injuries sustained while wearing it. Therefore, if you manage to land an attack, a battle of endurance will be in effect......
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the explanation in a calm, factual tone, with a slight emphasis on key points.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But with Badigadi as the opponent, that becomes impossible.

The Fighting God Armor will continue to move until its wearer dies.

Badigadi is immortal.

In other words, perpetual motion.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, deliberate pace, emphasizing the gravity of the situation.

annotated.text: How did Laplace defeat it?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Ask the question with a tone of curiosity and mild confusion.

annotated.text: He overwhelmed the defensive limits of the Fighting God Armor by hitting it with a spell with a massive output, temporary annihilating the contents, and separating them. As a result, a large hole opened up in the continent and the Rings Sea was created.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak in a clear, informative tone, explaining the events with a calm and measured delivery.

annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Respond with a quiet, contemplative tone, showing understanding.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Depending on the power of the attack, it was possible to deal damage.

It was just a matter of his recovery after that.

But if it was so, then this gives us one plan….
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, thoughtful pace, highlighting the implications of the information.

annotated.text: But I heard the wearer from that time died. So it was Badigadi.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of realization and mild surprise.

annotated.text: You didn't know?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the statement with a calm, reflective tone, showing a mix of resignation and curiosity.

annotated.text: Laplace, at that time, also didn't seem to know who was wearing it. After I heard about his death, I lost my remaining interest. Since I never would’ve thought that the Fighting God would appear before me like this.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Ask the question with a hesitant, uncertain tone, as if unsure of the answer.

annotated.text: Did you........hear it from Laplace himself in a previous loop?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a confident, assertive tone, emphasizing the speaker's identity and authority.

annotated.text: That's right. I am the son of the First Generation Dragon God. First Generation Dragon God also instructed me on how to apply this curse.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Voice is hesitant and questioning, showing some confusion or doubt.

annotated.text: ....But you said that Laplace must be killed.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a calm, resolute tone, delivering the information with clarity and certainty.

annotated.text: That’s right. To reach the place where Hitogami is, the five Dragon Generals must be killed and the sacred treasures retrieved.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, deliberate pace, emphasizing the significance of the moment.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I think this is the first time that I've heard him say clearly that they must be killed.

So it’s like that after all.

Then I guess we really can’t count on Perugius's support after all. I also wouldn't want to help someone who has the intention of betraying me later on.

But I guess there's no benefit in discussing that here.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a reflective, slightly bitter tone, expressing frustration and resignation.

annotated.text: This is probably an unpleasant conversation for you.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a quiet, apologetic tone, acknowledging the discomfort of the conversation.

annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Voice is firm and resolute, showing determination and focus on the immediate challenge.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Right now, I have to think about what's in front of me.

That is, Badigadi.

If Hitogami was acting while seeing his own future, then he couldn’t freely move such a chess piece like Badigadi, who acted selfishly.

Or this might even be the final trump card that Hitogami held.

When I saw him a few days ago, he seemed to be at his wits’ end.

Fighting God Badigadi.

Badigadi was originally Hitogami's apostle.

It was unknown to me just why Hitogami didn’t use Badi until this loop, but let’s consider that he was suddenly dragged out this time.

Well, if he didn’t come out in any of the previous loops, then I would have to be the cause.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, deliberate pace, emphasizing the weight of the situation and the stakes involved.

annotated.text: So what do you intend to do?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Ask the question with a tone of curiosity and urgency, seeking a clear answer.

annotated.text: Fight. There is no escape.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a determined, resolute tone, showing commitment and confidence.

annotated.text: Alright. I'll come. I haven't done it before, but it shouldn’t be something that we can’t do.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Deliver the statement with a calm, confident tone, showing readiness and resolve.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As Orsted said that, he started getting up.

However, I interrupted him.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a firm, urgent tone, interrupting the previous speaker with authority.

annotated.text: No, please wait.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Speak with a polite, apologetic tone, showing deference and respect.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Orsted sat back down.

I couldn’t see his face because of the mask, but I could understand that he probably had an astonished expression.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after the first sentence.

annotated.text: If Orsted-sama were to exhaust his mana here, it would be a defeat overall. There wouldn't be any meaning.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Authoritative, calm tone with a hint of internal conflict.

annotated.text: If you die here, it would also result in defeat. There wouldn't be any meaning.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Same as previous, with a slight hesitation before the final phrase.

annotated.text: ......Well, that's also true.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Slight pause after the ellipsis, followed by a resigned tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Should we take the chance now or take it later?

But I've tried my best until now.

I wanted to at least stick through until I think it was truly impossible.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a rising inflection at the end.

annotated.text: But even if Orsted-sama must fight, before then, it should still be possible to weaken the Fighting God.
annotated.speaker: GISU
annotated.instruct: Calm, measured tone with a subtle emphasis on the word 'die'.

annotated.text: ...You'll die.
annotated.speaker: GISU
annotated.instruct: Same as previous, with a more subdued and somber delivery.

annotated.text: If that happens, then please take care of my remaining family members.
annotated.speaker: GISU
annotated.instruct: Slightly emotional, with a soft emphasis on 'family members'.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I don't want to die. I want to return back alive.

But this was definitely a do or die situation.

The Fighting God was Hitogami and Gisu's final card.

There might still be another card, but in this situation, the Dark King, Sword God, North God, and Ogre God have all been defeated.

There's only one apostle left too.

All of his cards were in the open.

There were no more cards to pull out.

If we defeated the Fighting God here, the other side should suffer in turn.

We must persevere, fight and take the victory.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a rising tone at the end.

annotated.text: I understand. But as soon as you realize that you can’t win, retreat immediately. Understood?
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Calm, authoritative tone with a slight urgency.

annotated.text: Thank you very much.
annotated.speaker: GISU
annotated.instruct: Soft, sincere tone with a brief pause before the final word.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I bowed my head and stood up.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after the action.

annotated.text: So........Did Roxy contact you yet?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Curious, hesitant tone with a trailing off at the end.

annotated.text: Not yet.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Calm, measured tone with a slight emphasis on 'immediately'.

annotated.text: Is that so. When it happens, please let me know immediately.
annotated.speaker: ORSTED
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a rising tone as the text builds tension.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
After I saw Orsted nod, I got out of the house.

The soldiers were waiting.

With a sharp glint in her eye, radiating bloodlust was Eris.

Standing with a clear bearing was Ruijerd.

The slightly nervous, scared, and excited Cliff.

With an expression that wanted to protect Cliff was Elinalise.

Sad after hearing of Sándor's defeat, the weeping Doga.

Having lost all his clothes during the previous battle, he was wearing the Supard's local dress, Zanoba.

And the Supard warriors aiming to protect the village.

This group.

Honestly, I'm uneasy.

The gap left by Sándor, Atofe, and Malta was huge.

But Zanoba and Doga were a good replacement for the Ogre God.

Badigadi was a close combat type. The compatibility wasn’t bad.

They were inferior to the Ogre God. Even if their compatibility wasn’t bad, it was unknown just how much meaning that held.

It was possible that this group would be able to stall for time for 2 days, or at least 1 day.

And within that 1 or 2 days, the possibility of my trump card arriving was low.

Then, there was no guarantee whether or not I would win even while using my trump card.

But it was possible that my comrades would just die in vain.
annotated.instruct: Calm, determined tone with a slight urgency.

annotated.text: Let’s go.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a trailing off at the end.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
However, I walked nonetheless.

I had a plan, but no chance of success.

I couldn’t even guarantee whether my decision was right.

We might have some time to lay traps, but the enemy wasn’t someone who would be defeated from just that.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a brief pause.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Everyone, without expressing any opinions, simply followed behind me.

I will fight the Fighting God.

Author's Q&A

Q. Was the reason that the Ogre God’s speech was crude and that he didn’t use Demon God Language while negotiating because there were people around him who didn’t understand Demon God Language?

→ The Ogre God who was an Ogre who surrendered to Rudi who was a human. That’s why he thought that talking in Human Language to respect the winner were obvious manners.

A. That’s how it is!

Q. If the President was fighting the one who was wearing the armor, then his words that the Fighting God never once stood in his way as an enemy was a little strange.

A. This is a little difficult, but bear with me. In short, he meant that he hadn’t fought anyone at the level of the 3rd World Power wearing the Fighting God armor.

Q. The President knows nearly everything, it’s like he’s Wikipedia-sensei or Google-sensei. And the lithograph looked like his Twitter.

A. You’ll often get
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight shift in tone for the 'Author's Q&A' section.

annotated.text: This article does not exist
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause before the final line.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
.

Q. An inertia game is better than Arcana Heart, you know!

If it’s a fighting game with fighting in the sky while ignoring inertia, then I guess a Touhou like game system is close to it.

A. They don’t have floating steps in that image.

Q. The person who wears the Fighting God armor becomes the Fighting God? Or His Majesty Badi who wears the Fighting God armor is the Fighting God?

A. The latter.

Among the SGWP, it becomes a somewhat special type of pattern.

Q. If the conditions for the change in SGWP monument is losing consciousness or death, then when the abstinent Rudeus carelessly reached his hand out to Eris’s mountain range and was knocked out with one punch, would it change then?

A. When they realized, the Seventh rank was changed to a Sword God Style mark!

Q. When the city was annihilated, I got the image that it disappeared without leaving any traces. Shouldn’t it be collapsed or destroyed? Or was it literally annihilated?

Why, in a hand-to-hand battle, was the city was annihilated?

A. It’s the result of normal hand-to-hand combat and the support that Moore and the rest provided using magic for a long period of time.

At the very least, it was possibly annihilated.

Q. When Orsted wore the Fighting God Armor, was he unable to take it off until he died?

A. Yes. He died right there and then looped.

Q. It feels like the President’s mana capacity absolutely can’t be charged by outside factors. Would there be no other choice in future other than normal self-recovery?

A. This......might be researched by someone in the future.

Q. A God Rank for a swordsman has made an appearance but a God Rank for a mage has yet to come out. And someone with a God Rank Magic who can cure the Magic Stone Disease hasn’t come out yet either…...this work is going to be over soon, but does that mean they will never appear?

A. Probably never.

Q. It has become such a desperate situation, but there’s still not that much bloodshed yet.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a rising tone as the text builds tension.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: How come there’s no fight scene either!?
annotated.instruct: Exasperated, with a rising tone at the end.

annotated.text: A. Let’s see.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Calm, reflective tone with a slight pause.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I did write that Rudeus fell unconscious. I should’ve depicted it with more depth I guess.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a trailing off at the end.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Q. After fighting the Fighting God, literally everyone’s still alive (expect those who are still missing). Does that mean that Badi is going easy on them?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight questioning tone.

annotated.text: A. Even without wearing armor, it may be that the rest of the guys are at a level where it would be hard to kill them instantly.
annotated.speaker: BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Confident and calm, with a touch of dry humor.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Q. But Orsted should’ve disposed of the Fighting God Armor.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight questioning tone.

annotated.text: A. When performing a speedrun in an RPG, the strongest most powerful weapon was in an extremely deep labyrinth. It’s not required to defeat the Last Boss, and hence there was no need to get it... something like that.
annotated.speaker: BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Confident and calm, with a touch of dry humor.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: There was a time when he tried it once for trial and error, but he thought that it was unreasonable and wasted a lot of mana (just hitting with the Godsword is fine), and so he didn’t use it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly exasperated tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: And for someone who doesn’t want to be famous and stand out in the world for getting it, it’s quite unreasonable.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly exasperated tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Chapter 257: Trump Card
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Part 1
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The Fighting God appeared after two days.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It was thanks to Atofe and the others holding him back.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But they didn't return.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I didn’t think that the Immortal Demon race would die that easily......but the Fighting God probably did enough damage so that they couldn’t follow.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: In any case, thanks to them, our preparations were complete.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The Fighting God came at us head on.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Without hiding or rushing.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Calmly, he made an appearance.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Gisu was sitting on his shoulder.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: As if to say that no matter what we did, we couldn’t stop him.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Part 2
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The battle began at the entrance of the forest.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I was standing at the top of a giant wall created at the entrance of the forest.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It was about 10 meters high and 2 meters wide.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: From the top of this wall, which was made as if to protect the forest, I would be hurling magic. Stone cannons.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I would hurl quite a number of them so that I could at least knock down Gisu.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The clairvoyance eye didn’t work against Badigadi.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly dramatic tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It seemed that even Orsted didn’t know the reason. Badigadi was probably just that kind of Miko, or as a result of something in the past, he obtained resistance to those Demon eyes.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after mentioning Orsted's uncertainty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The Gold gleamed in the far distance.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a subtle emphasis on the gleaming gold.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: On top of that, ever since I was born into this world, stone cannon had been the spell I had used the most.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a reflective tone about the speaker's reliance on stone cannon.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I aimed for a direct hit.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a focused delivery on the act of aiming.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: 1 in every 10 shots made it hit.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a measured tone highlighting the low success rate.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But, even from this distance, I understood that it didn’t do much damage.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight concern in the voice about the damage inflicted.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: A direct hit would open a hole in the Golden Armor, but it would quickly be filled again.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a clear explanation of the armor's resilience.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It didn’t penetrate.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a definitive tone about the lack of penetration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Even stalling him was a failure, the Fighting God continued forward without even defending himself.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of frustration at the failure to stall the enemy.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: At this distance, there seemed to be a drop in power.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight observation about the power drop at distance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: As I thought, it’d have to be at close range.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a decisive tone about the need for close range.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Incidentally, one also hit Gisu.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a casual mention of the incidental hit on Gisu.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It was hard to see from this distance, but he fell off from the shoulder when it hit, so I’m pretty sure that it hit him.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a detailed and calm explanation of Gisu's resilience.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But he got up as if nothing had happened, so it seemed he took almost no damage.

He may have simply gotten off Fighting God’s shoulder as a measure of precaution and went around the back.

If he was a bit closer, Gisu might have taken enough damage to cause instant death.

But when you think about how he wasn’t annihilated by the thunderfall, it looked like Gisu himself also had some kind of magic resistance.

In the end, we couldn’t even halt his advance.

When the Fighting God got close enough, I casted fire magic towards the exteriors of wall and retreated into the forest.

I didn’t have any intention to let him get any closer than necessary.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and methodical delivery of the strategy and retreat.

annotated.text: So far it's within expectations.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Calm, confident tone with a slight smirk, expressing satisfaction with the situation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Once I confirmed the destruction of the wall, a mutter leaked from my mouth.

Within expectations.

I knew that this would happen.

When the Fighting God entered the forest, the entire forest was covered in a wide and dense fog by me.

While activating a quagmire of the same size.

Reconnaissance and spreading confusion were entrusted to a force of Supard warriors led by Ruijerd.

Magic eyes didn’t seem to be effective against him, but the Supards' third eye was; their senses could catch the Fighting God.

It was effective.

According to the report, as a result of the Supards' guerrilla warfare, the Fighting God had lost his way, and had been wandering aimlessly for a couple hours.

I hoped that he continued to wander around like this and end up at the exit to the forest.

While hoping that, I continued to extend the range of the fog and quagmire.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a detailed and calm explanation of the fog and quagmire strategy.

annotated.text: The Fighting God has changed his direction.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Calm, authoritative tone with a slight concern about the Fighting God's direction change.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
And with that timing, Ruijerd appeared to report.

It seemed the Fighting God was now moving right towards the Earth Dragon Valley.

This was probably Gisu's contribution.

Rather than Badigadi alone, it seemed Gisu knew how to walk inside a forest with a fog this dense.

The question arises whether he could still walk even if he knew the way, but if one considers that he used some kind of Magic Tool or Magic Item, then it wouldn’t be strange to think otherwise.

No, if he had a magic tool, then he wouldn't have wandered around for hours like that.

Amongst the mud and the dense fog, he probably had to use some anachronistic way, taking his time and then deciding on one path.

The fog, quagmire, and the Supards’ guerrilla warfare.

Even with all that, we were only able to stall him for three hours.

There were a total of three casualties.

Three Supard warriors who got too close, were done in by the Fighting God.

But their deaths were not in vain.

Thanks to them, the sun had gone down.

And at the same time, the Fighting God's movements had stopped.

Although it was probably not solar powered, it seemed he stopped moving during the night.

But I did not stop.

I didn’t loosen the effect of the Fog or Quagmire, nor did the Supards stop their guerrilla warfare.

A long distance attack with exploding stone cannons was thrown at him.

I wasn’t expecting much damage.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a determined tone about continuing the attack.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But I would simply not let them sleep, I would keep firing to not let them rest.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight emphasis on the significance of the attack on Gisu.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It may not have much effect on Badigadi, but to Gisu it had meaning.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a reflective tone about the end of the first day.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: With those thoughts, the first day ended.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a clear and concise transition to part 3.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Part 3
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a determined tone about luring the Fighting God.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: On the second day, continuing what I was doing during the latter half of the first day, we tried with all our might to lure the Fighting God to the Earth Dragon Valley.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight emphasis on the dawn of the second day.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Dawn of the second day.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a focused tone about crossing the valley.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I crossed the valley.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a commanding tone about glaring down at the forest.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: From on top of the rampart, I glared down at the forest.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight edge of determination.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Standing next to me was Ruijerd looking out in the same way.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm, observational tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The topography of the Earth Dragon Valley was extremely well suited for defense.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a factual, informative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It was a chasm more than 1km deep.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a matter-of-fact tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I didn’t notice it when I first crossed it but the cliff on Supard’s village side was slightly higher.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a reflective, analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It doesn't have much to do with magic, but fundamentally, a higher position in battle is advantageous.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a logical, explanatory tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: One could see better from an elevated position, and with gravity working against you, it would take more energy to go uphill than down.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a practical, tactical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: With that mindset, I created a rampart with earth magic from the depths of the cliff at the side of the Supard’s village.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a confident, assertive tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It was a little less than 20 meters high, so it's not as wide as the one at the entrance to the forest, but this was the only place that the valley was quite narrow, so it's not a problem.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a measured, precise tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I had opened a hole in it where the bridge was connected as an entrance, but I closed it up after I dropped the bridge.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a strategic, calculated tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: This way, he couldn’t just jump across and suddenly start the battle like the Ogre God did......probably.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a cautious, speculative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I never thought lightly of the Fighting God, but this was the strongest and highest wall I could prepare in such short time.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a resolute, determined tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: If he could jump over this, I'd have to give up on it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a pragmatic, resigned tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Even if he didn’t jump across, and simply arrived at the surface of the wall, it was possible to pelt him with the stone cannons from above.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tactical, informed tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: He could render magic invalid, but he could not reverse terrain changes, I was now aware of that during the previous battle.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a reflective, analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Again, because of the confirmation I got at the start of the battle, I realized that stone cannons were sufficiently effective.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a confident, assured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: If they were to cling to this wall and I hit Gisu with the stone cannon from the top of this wall, then Gisu, who didn’t possess any power at all, will fall into the valley.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a strategic, calculated tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: If not, then it should be possible to create a large quantity of water over the top of them, making them slip and fall into the valley.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a pragmatic, logical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Gisu may be a useful guy, but in a straight up fight, he's powerless.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a balanced, objective tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Still, Badi was someone who was good at executing strategy and Gisu was someone who was proficient at making strategies from his ingenuity.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a respectful, admiring tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: They have the greatest compatibility.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a neutral, factual tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: There was also a risk in leading him to this narrow stretch of valley.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a cautious, measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But it was better than him crossing the valley by himself in some place I don't know and attacking from that side.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a pragmatic, decisive tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: At the top of the valley were Cliff, Ruijerd, the Supard warriors, and me.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a detailed, informative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The remaining Supard warriors were stationed somewhere off the wall for surveillance.

Worst case scenario, if he crossed the valley somewhere other than here, we would know immediately.

Right behind the rampart, Eris and the rest were on standby.

If they broke through here, it would be an all out war.

We managed to buy some time.

What would have been a one day trip in a straight line took three.

We earned two days.

There still hadn't been any contact from Roxy.

The time we bought might have been pointless, but I don't have any intention of changing our decision to buy time.

From the battle at the port city, we understood that we can't win in a straight up fight.

I have to bet on my trump card.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a contemplative, resolute tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Dawn arrived.

We did not know when he would arrive.

I was looking over the forest with the Supard warriors. According to their observations, the enemy camp was outside their range.

I wasn’t sure of what to think.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.text: .......They’re here!
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Sudden, urgent shout with a panicked and alarmed tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As I was thinking that, Ruijerd called out.

Looking at the dim forest, I strained my eyes to the best of my ability.

I could see it.

It’s only the size of a speck, but someone was standing in the forest.

But it’s not gold.

It was someone in a white robe.

I recognized the feeling that robe gave off.

It was Gisu.

It was possible that it may be someone else, but it looked like Gisu.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.text: Who’s that?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Confused, questioning tone with a hint of uncertainty.

annotated.text: Gisu.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Short, definitive statement with a confident and authoritative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Ruijerd looked hard and confirmed it.

From here to there was within the range of the third eye.

Therefore, the probability of it being Gisu was high.

Not from the bare edge of the valley, but from deep into the forest, he was making his way to us through the thicket.

It was difficult to see since it was still dark, but it definitely looked like Gisu.

But the Golden color couldn’t be seen near him.

Gisu was alone.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.text: Huh?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Confused, questioning tone with a hint of uncertainty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Alone?

Was he scouting alone?

Gisu, who knew just what kind of magic I should be capable of casting, was alone?

Was he confident?

Or was Badigadi near him in standby?

No, he’s about 100 meters from the valley; if Badigadi was close enough to provide backup, Ruijerd would have been able to see him.

At this distance, shouldn’t my attack be able to kill him?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Thinking that, my heart began to beat faster.

The stone cannon will reach.

Gisu seems to be investigating over here, but I get the feeling he hasn’t noticed me yet.

I can hit him.

100 meters.

Taking into account the elevation, it can’t be more than 120m.

If aimed properly, I can definitely hit him at this distance.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Should I?

No, what would I do if it was someone else?

An adventurer wearing a white robe that just got lost in the forest.

.......No.

No one should’ve been able to even move because of the fog and quagmire from yesterday.

Someone couldn’t have come in this far.

If they were already this close to the valley before the battle started, then they would have already been picked up on the Supards’ radar.

Right now, I can defeat Gisu.

What should I do?

It has to be a trap.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But what kind of trap?

Right now, I could attack. What kind of card does the other side have?

If I attack, will he gain some kind of advantage?

Could it be that the person over there was someone who looked like Gisu?

Was it possible that it’s one of my allies or family?

No, it can’t be.

Impossible.

Up until yesterday, it was just the two of them.

Someone couldn’t just suddenly come along.

Isn’t this my chance?

Up until now, I have been focused primarily on buying time, I haven’t yet made an actual attack.

From the port until here, slowly advancing backwards.

On the journey with the carefree Badigadi, it’s possible that he thinks this might be an easy victory.

Was it unlikely that they let their guard down and ended up showing their faces here?

The attack would be very brief and the risk would be little.

Was there any reason not to attack?

There was the possibility that they had put a guy over there by some means or something that I wouldn’t want to kill.

But what was the meaning in doing something like that, strategically speaking?

What’s the meaning that I do not attack from here?

......Confusion.

It feels like a trap, but I couldn’t think of any demerits at the least if I attacked from here.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Alright.

Let’s shoot.

It may be a trap, but there’s no demerit in just shooting him.

I’ll just deal with it when the time comes.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.text: .......I’ll be attacking.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Short, affirmative response with a calm and confident tone.

annotated.text: Got it.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I concentrated mana in my right hand.

I stressed accuracy rather than speed or power.

I couldn't see him through the clairvoyance as usual, but I was changing the scenery using clairvoyance while predicting the impact by on-offing mana to the foresight eye.

An exploding stone cannon was used if it missed the target.

I hesitated for a moment at the brink of shooting.

But immediately after my moment of hesitation, the stone cannon got released from my finger. With an almost straight trajectory, it was sucked into the opposite side of the valley.

There was no sound.

After it impacted on the person at the opposite side of the valley, that person fell down as if a doll’s string was cut.

After that, he didn’t move.

It hit.

There was a response.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As if nothing had happened at all, time continued to flow as usual.

The fallen person wasn’t moving.

Within the morning glow, nothing could be heard other than the rustling noises of the forest.

10 minutes.

20 minutes.

No, the accurate passage of time was unknown, but time was simply moving nevertheless.

During that time, something sprouted within me.

(I want to confirm it)

I wanted to confirm just who was the person fallen there.

Was it Gisu or was it someone else?

Dead or not?

I’d quickly go there, confirm it, and then come back immediately.

Only that much is safe.

That thought born inside me.

But I sensed something at the same time.

This was the trap.

Attacking him wasn’t the trap, but this feeling that was budding within me right now was Gisu’s strategy.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
If the person fallen over there was really Gisu at the verge of dying, and it came to that finishing him off were the circumstances.

If the person fallen over there was Sylphy who was caught unnoticed and somehow they were able to fool Ruijerd’s eye, and we had to go there and save her immediately or else she would die.

When I go there, the Fighting God would appear and then I’ll be killed.

I must not go there.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
1 hour passed.

I was becoming nervous.

Did I do some kind of mistake that cannot be undone?

Should I not have fired after all?

Was their objective to make me shoot, and then stall me here?

Were they crossing the valley from some other place right now?

No, just in case, the warriors of the Supard race were keeping guard at various places of the valley.

I’ll believe in them.

2 hours passed.

Should I go there and confirm it after all?

After confirming, would I not be able to predict Gisu’s next move?

Could it be that I was running away from the act of confirming because of some kind of reasoning?

3 hours passed.

No movements whatsoever.

Various patterns came to mind.

I got tired of thinking so much already.

If making me tired in this way was Gisu’s strategy, then it was working.

4 hours passed.

That was a corpse.

If it didn’t move for 4 hours straight then I have no doubt that it was a corpse.

But I wonder just whose corpse it is.

Gisu was dead, but it was likely Badigadi wasn’t moving.

If Roxy were here at a time like this, then I could’ve heard some kind of constructive opinion from her.

Cliff was just shaking his head with a sullen face.

6 hours passed.

After having a light lunch, we continued to gaze at the corpse.

It didn’t move.

8 hours passed.

It was soon mid-afternoon.

The day was gradually passing.

As a result of bracing myself for so long, I was now starting to get tired.

If, if nothing happened after the day had been completely passed, I would be going out there to confirm it.

10 hours passed.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.text: Rudeus, he’s here.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a calm and measured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
On Ruijerd’s words, I looked at the forest, taken aback.

From there, an armor glittering with golden color was coming out of the forest.

When the golden armor approached the corpse, he slowly stood up.

And then after they faced each other and talked about something, he faced this way.

When he shrugged his shoulders, I realized.

That gesture was, without a doubt, Gisu’s.

They quickly returned back deep into the forest.

And then silence arrived for a short while again.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Exhausted sigh, voice trembling slightly.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
So it was a trap.

That was Gisu.

He made himself a decoy to lure me to him.

That was dangerous.

Still, after a little more and it will be night.

I’ll entrust the Supard warriors over here with the look out and then sleep myself a little bit.

I was too tired.

It wasn’t likely that they could come at night, but let’s make it a quick nap regardless.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: I’ll be sleeping for a short while.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Soft, tired whisper.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
While thinking that, I wrapped myself up with a blanket.

The 3rd day was over.

Part 4
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The night of 3rd day.

It seemed the opposing side was in a bind after looking at the rampart.

They couldn’t just try to leap over the rampart.

And if they couldn’t leap over then there was no way to protect Gisu, that thought hit me.

I could understand that because a stone came flying from the other side.

It was a pretty big stone at first.

Even as that came at such an alarmingly fast rate that we got goosebumps, it impacted the wall and one part of it was destroyed.

After that, logs and stones came flying towards us at a terrific speed, which were all intercepted by me, who was startled by the banging roars, and we were able to avoid collateral on the rampart.

If they didn’t do something about the wall, then they couldn’t break through.

That was probably why they were acting like this.

Not to mention, looking at Badigadi’s fighting style until now, he could’ve easily broken through here if he was alone, even if it was something impossible.

So it was Gisu after all.

If he left Gisu behind, then he could break through.

But it was possible that someone would pursue him from the back, taking Gisu’s life.

Of course, there was nothing like reinforcements coming from outside the forest........

But it was possible that Atofe would revive and come chasing after them.

They were possibly afraid about this matter.

Even if that was not true, then just leaving one Supard warrior on the forest side would be sufficient for the job.

.......But it could be possible that was exposed yesterday.

Even if there’s a watchguard in my absence, it would be a quick story.

It wouldn’t be surprising if Fighting God leaped over here alone any time now.

And then........no reinforcements came.

Part 5

The fourth day.

The Fighting God arrived along with the sunrise.

Alone, as I had expected.

While running with long jumps similar to Malta.

And clung near the bottom of the walls.

As I had expected.

Yes, as I had expected.

Gisu wasn’t riding on his back.

The moment I confirmed that, I faced towards the opposite side of the valley and fired magic.

A wide range
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Flashover
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Sharp, commanding tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
.

The forest was engulfed in fire in an instant.

The effective range was unknown.

But there was no time to confirm it.

While dedicating a fraction of my vision towards the forest fire, I concentrated on the enemy in front of me.

The Fighting God made good use of his 6 arms to quickly climb up the wall like a spider.

In order to knock him off, Cliff and I fired stone cannons and water balls in large amounts, but it was in vain.

The Fighting God ran up the surface of the wall with overwhelming speed.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Cliff! It’s useless, retreat! Ruijerd-san! I’ll leave it up to you!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Urgent, panicked voice.

annotated.text: Got it!
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Quick, affirmative response.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Ruijerd took the two of us and jumped down the rampart.

Of course, I didn’t wait for Fighting God to pass over the rampart.

The moment we landed, I used magic and knocked down the rampart.

The huge rampart fell towards the valley.

It was futile.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The slowly falling rampart blew up like a dynamite being used.

The huge stones flew into the air.

A golden armor was flying within them.

The stones poured like rain.

While dealing with them with my magic, I didn’t take my eyes off from the Fighting God.

The Fighting God landed nearby me, a spot 5 metres away from me.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Hmm. Hmm.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Confused, hesitant mutter.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: And then he slowly turned towards us.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Now then, once again.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deep, booming voice with authority.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
With his upper arms folding themselves, the middle arm pointing towards me and the lower arms being put on his waist.

Badigadi saw me.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: My name is Fighting God Badigadi! The one who has taken the name of the Fighting God only as a sworn friend of Hitogami! I challenge you bastard to a personal duel!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Fierce, defiant tone.

annotated.text: I WANT TO ASK ABOUT ONE THING BEFORE THAT!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I shouted at once.

While putting aside the thought that there would be no use in arguing, I still shouted.
annotated.instruct: Angry, demanding voice.

annotated.text: Your Majesty Badi, just why are you supporting Hitogami!? What does it mean to be a sworn friend!? Were you not deceived by Hitogami before!?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: He certainly deceived me! I was deceived when in order to protect Kishirika, I tried to kill Laplace by wearing this armor, but I killed Laplace and ended up murdering Kishirika as well!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Angry, demanding voice.

annotated.text: Then, just why!?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Hitogami apologized to me about that time by bowing to me! And on top of that, he requested me for my cooperation! Thus the Great I couldn’t say no to him!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Hitogami apologized?

That’s a lie.

I couldn’t think of him apologizing of all things.

Even if he apologized, it would be like
annotated.instruct: Mocking, sarcastic tone.

annotated.text: Ahaha, that time was my bad, ‘kay
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: while grinning.
annotated.instruct: Deliver with a playful, teasing tone, as if sharing a private joke.

annotated.text: He’s deceiving you again!
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Speak with sharp, accusatory intensity, voice rising in urgency.

annotated.text: Don’t care! Even if he deceives me, as long as he keeps apologizing, I’ll just keep forgiving him! The Great I, am immortal! Kishirika resurrected too! Even if he apologized now, there’s no longer any source of resent! He may wish for anything even more than this!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Exude arrogant confidence, mixing boastful bravado with a hint of self-satisfaction.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He’s too lenient.

It felt like he was saying some very good things.

Even I might let it go if it was a trivial lie.

But I couldn’t convince myself that killing my family was something trivial.

I wasn’t one of the Immortal Demon Clan. My common sense was different.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a measured, reflective tone, conveying internal conflict and moral weight.

annotated.text: Would you not think about changing sides?
annotated.speaker: BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Speak with a commanding, almost mocking tone, suggesting a challenge and a test of will.

annotated.text: Futile! I was never on the Dragon God’s side to begin with! But, if you were to gain victory in this battle, I will think about it!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deliver with dramatic flair, emphasizing defiance and reluctant concession.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Fight and then convey your desire.

This part of him resembled Atofe a lot.

If I recall, it was also a duel when I first met this Demon Lord.

Did I win that time or did I lose?

At the very least, it ended with Badigadi acknowledging my strength.

That’s why, he might have gotten along well with me.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, observational tone, drawing parallels and reflecting on past events.

annotated.text: .......I understand. I will accept Your Majesty’s challenge.
annotated.speaker: BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Speak with a solemn, resolute tone, showing acceptance of a challenge.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But the declaration this time.

Badigadi had forgotten a few words.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slightly amused, almost wry tone, hinting at a forgotten detail.

annotated.text: We’ll fight Your Majesty with everyone here.
annotated.speaker: BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Speak with a firm, determined tone, showing unity and collective resolve.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Eris, Elinalize, Zanoba, and Doga showed up from the thicket behind me.

Furthermore, many warriors of the Supard race, who were standing guard near the valley, gathered one by one.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a dramatic, escalating tone, building tension and anticipation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: And thus, an all-out war began.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a neutral, matter-of-fact tone, signaling a transition or division.
