annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Even so, I cut the mana supply to the clairvoyance, and by looking at my comrade’s movements through the foresight eye, I could in turn predict his movements.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly contemplative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Doing something like this was a first for me.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of mild surprise.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I hadn’t practiced using it nor was trained to use it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly hesitant tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But I was somehow able to do it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of mild confidence.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I was able to understand my comrade’s movements as well as the enemy’s within this battle while closing one of my eyes.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly focused and intense tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: In fact, it went smoother than when I usually went about doing such things.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly relaxed and smooth tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I wonder if it was only because of the pivotal support of my allies.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly questioning and reflective tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Or is it because of Badigadi’s frank movements?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly curious and contemplative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: At least, Badigadi didn’t have Alek’s level of skill.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly comparative and analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Despite being surrounded by Eris, Ruijerd, and Sándor, Alek kept fighting with almost no injuries.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly surprised and impressed tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But Badigadi was different.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly contrasting and analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The number of people was different this time around, but his body was getting hit by almost all of our attacks.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly descriptive and observational tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Things were progressing well.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly confident and assured tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: I could properly see the enemy’s movements and could predict them as well.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly uncertain and contemplative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Nevertheless, a winning vision doesn’t come to mind.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly factual and observational tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Badigadi was receiving all of our attacks.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly reflective and analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But that’s just it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly emphatic and descriptive tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Even if Eris cut him, even if Ruijerd pierced him, it quickly repaired itself.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly vivid and descriptive tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: The golden armor crawled like a living being and filled up the holes in an instant.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly analytical and speculative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Probably restoration was taking place even inside the armor.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly surprising and observational tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: At first it looked like we were giving him a lot of damage, but he wasn’t getting any damage at all.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly contrasting and analytical tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: And he wasn’t getting fatigued as well.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly comparative and reflective tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: At first it looked like we would gain easy victory, but fatigue wasn’t even getting accumulated like in Alek’s case.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of growing concern, emphasizing the contrast between expected fatigue and the unexpected endurance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: It felt like the fight would just keep on continuing forever, and our side was getting in an unfavourable position.
annotated.instruct: Convey a sense of mounting dread and inevitability, with a slow, heavy delivery.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: We had no chance of winning.
annotated.instruct: Speak with a tone of grim resignation, highlighting the futility of the situation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: We were just holding out.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a steady, detailed pace, describing the battle's progression with clinical detachment.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Until this battle formation reached its limits, until someone suddenly collapsed, we were simply holding out till then.

It had been a few hours since our clash, yet we held out.

We didn’t know what would happen if we held out like this, but we simply held out.

But it seemed forced nonetheless.

As expected, the first to go down were the Supard warriors.

They were, by no means, weak.

But many were inferior compared to Ruijerd.

It was because these people simply hadn’t fought enough real battles.

Or it was possible that these warriors were the ones who weren’t born during the time of Laplace’s military campaign.

These warriors who, since the time of their birth, only hunted the Invisible wolves and nothing else, couldn’t keep up with the Fighting God’s battle.

They fell one by one from the battlefield just like the falling dominoes.

There were those who clearly died instantly, those who were serious injured but still fought, and those who remained indistinct.

In the end, a group of more than 10 warriors was reduced to only 3.

The one to go down next was Elinalize.

She was also, by no means at all, weak.

She was practically one of the top class among the adventurers.

She was on a level where she could become a vanguard during the capture of a S-class labyrinth.

But that was still among the adventurers.

Her specialty was her skillful use of a shield to ward off attacks, and from there with as little injuries as possible she was able to control the soldiers that would be prevalent.

But the shield that she was accustomed to wasn’t with her.

Although she warded off most of Fighting God Badigadi’s attacks with her skills by making use of the shield I made using Earth Magic, it was still easily penetrated.

Elinalize danced in mid-air and was slapped into a large tree, rendering her unconsciousness.

It started collapsing from that point onwards.

When Elinalize fainted, Cliff’s mind was preoccupied by her.

During that little window, he was dragged up into the Fighting God’s charge.

As if hit by a truck, Cliff was blown off into a thicket and vanished.

Was it instant death or a grave injury? There wasn’t any distinction, but he wasn’t returning.

After that, I had no doubt that he had lost consciousness.

When Cliff fainted, Zanoba and Doga who were receiving healing magic from him lost their support.

They who were struck by the attacks only a few times because of my stone cannons as support and with Elinalize’s backing, were now getting struck by almost all of the attacks.

They were still able to hold out for some more because of my healing magic, but that was it.

Catching up with the two of them who were getting blown each time they were hit, and sending them out after casting healing magic was impossible for me.

If I had been wearing some equipment of Magic Armor

then it might’ve been possible.

We gradually lost our timing and the two of them were blown off simultaneously.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
After that, he took aim at Eris, due to which Ruijerd covered up for her and became unfit to fight.

I hurriedly healed Doga and ran to Zanoba’s side, but it was too late.

Our front had already started to crumble as quickly as Doga was blown away. And when I was healing Zanoba, what I saw at the corner of my eyes was Eris getting a direct hit by Fighting God’s fist.

Eris fell while vomiting blood.

That was fatal. My brain shouted that if I didn’t heal her immediately, it would be too late.

But I was too late.

Fighting God closed the distance between me and Zanoba.
annotated.instruct: Deliver the line with a sudden, mechanical tone, as if a machine or unknown entity is speaking.

annotated.text: UUOOOOoooooooooo!
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Zanoba howled.

He caught Fighting God’s upper right fist and then upper left fist.

He was punched in the stomach with the lower right fist and his body bent in a 90°.

While being punched in the head by the middle right fist, he was blown away horizontally.

And then the Fighting God approached me.

When I thought it was dangerous, it was too late.

I fired a shockwave with my right hand and when I moved back because of the recoil, I was already being hit.

His middle right fist approached me.

I quickly thought of guarding myself with my arms, but it was futile.

I was hit by a shockwave that felt like it could tear off my upper body and was blown away.

Was it good luck that I didn’t fell unconscious?

Or was it misfortune?

I could feel all of the bones from my shoulder to my ribs getting broken.

It was possible that even my spine broke since I could no longer feel my lower body.

Her actions were fluent and accurate.

The Fighting God’s attack, which was quite capable of dealing a one hit instant kill, looked like the tantrum of a child in front of that skill.

Of course, but of course, he wouldn’t go down with just that.

No matter how many times and how strong the counter she fired towards the Fighting God, even when she cut his arms or legs, there was no damage.

If she were to fight him one-on-one, she may put up a good fight, but she still wouldn’t be able to stand victorious at the very end.

I threw it strongly.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Fuahahaha! Useless, useless!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Maniacal, mocking laughter with a deep, booming voice.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
As Badigadi said that, his arm began to regrow.

It popped out like a certain person from N○mek.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Mngh.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Pained, strained grunt.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But it’s quite apparent that it wasn’t useless.

The arm that grew back was bare.

The armor wasn’t attached to it.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Oh, so that’s how it is.....you’ve thought things through!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Realization, slightly surprised tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Where I had thrown his arm just now...

I had prepared a certain magic circle over there.

Within it, Badigadi’s arm and the Fighting God Armor couldn’t regenerate.

It also seemed that Badigadi’s size had decreased somewhat.

I hadn’t actually thought about it.

But I got a hint.

Fighting God Badigadi.

Due to his armour, he possessed both high speed and power.

But his speed, compared to the sword masters I’ve faced before, was nothing special.

Orsted, and even Alek, were probably faster.

Although, obviously, he’s faster than me, when wearing the Magic Armor, it was at a level that I could compete with.

It’s thanks to the training that I’ve received from Eris and Orsted that I was still alive.

What’s troublesome was his ridiculously high defense and durability.

The Fighting God Armor was hard.

It could be boasted that it was even harder than the Magic Armor.

At the very least, if Eris and the others were to hit it with all their might, it would leave a scratch, but the arm or head parts might not get separated.

The armor would instantly restore itself and would keep on fighting as if nothing had happened.

Normally, that would cause damage to accumulate on the inside......

But on the Immortal Demon Lord Badigadi, it does not.

Eris’s slash or Ruijerd’s thrust would normally cause damage on the inside of the armor.

But with Badigadi, it didn’t cause that damage.

Whether it’s a slash or a thrust or a strike, it’s immediately healed.

Before long, the ones who were attacking would become tired, and they would inevitably succumb to the destructive power of those 6 arms.

Then, just how should he be brought down?

This hint laid with Atofe.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Immortal Demon Lord Atofe.

The symbol of fear itself for the various Demon Lords of the Demon Continent. The one who would keep getting up no matter how many times she was brought down and would keep charging towards the enemy.

There were two methods in order to bring her down.

The first was to disconnect the limbs and seal them so that they can’t be restored.

This was the most standard way and Atofe was defeated 2 times using this method in the past.

A barrier which was fit to seal them for hundreds of years would be required, but for now, simply surrounding the parts in an advanced level magic barrier was enough to stop regeneration.

The other way was to make her admit defeat.

The Immortal Demon Lord Atofe, in accordance with her own rule, would fight many opponents.

And so, by that rule, when she realizes that she has lost, she will admit defeat.

Although I didn’t think that it would be a simple matter to make the current Badigadi admit defeat.

So this time, I’d have to go with the former.

For this purpose, Cliff prepared various barrier magic circles throughout the forest.

They were set to activate when Badigadi’s limbs were thrown into them.

I was previously unsure about their effectiveness against the Fighting God Armor, but they were working.

Use the defense-ignoring sword to cut through the armor, separate the arms, and seal them.

By doing this 6 times, I could make Badigadi admit defeat.

I’d like to seal his whole body, but......without Cliff here, I couldn’t use the magic circle to seal his entire body.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: AAAAaaaaaa!
annotated.speaker: IMMORTAL DEMON LORD ATOFE
annotated.instruct: Agonized, high-pitched scream.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I charged at him while yelling.

I no longer cared about damage.

Not even I knew just how long the MK. Zero could run at full power.

Thanks to the Dragon King Sword, the operation time may have been extended to some extent, but it wouldn’t be strange if it stopped anytime soon.

There was no path besides a short and decisive battle.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: COME TO ME! HERO!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Fierce, commanding yell.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The Fighting God spreads his arms wide to my challenge.

And at the same time, he swung his right hand.

In response to the Fighting God's flying fist, I brandished my sword and prepared for a counter.

The movement of those six arms exceeded my expectations.

But I had already gotten used to it during the fight.

I was at my best today.

I could evade it.

I cut into the lower left arm.

At the same time, I aimed the shotgun at the cut and fired, blowing it apart.

But there was an unavoidable opening in that moment.

In the moment that I blew his arm away, I was hit by a fist and sent flying backwards.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Pained, breathless groan.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The surface of the Magic Armor cracked.

As expected, it couldn’t stand up to the Fighting God’s fist. But the arms not wearing any armor could be ignored.

Four more left.

The Magic armor only had to last until I send them all flying.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I noticed something else.

(The barrier is...)

The magic circle drawn on the ground was scraped off during that exchange.

From the aftermath of the battle.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
How did I not realize something so simple sooner?

Of course, there were still undamaged magic circles left, but I didn’t know which ones were still okay.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: ...Dammit!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I immediately threw away the arm I had cut.

I threw it into the Earth Dragon Valley.

The more beat up Atofe became, the longer it took her to revive, and if her beat up parts were spread out, she wouldn’t be able to revive immediately.

They could probably revive eventually, but it should have some meaning.

(...Hmm?)

For some reason, part of the armor wasn’t getting restored.

Did dismembering the user cause a loss in efficiency?

The restoration seemed to be slowing. Have the many years of not being used caused a drop in performance even in the Fighting God Armor?

Or was it Badigadi's strategy?

No, don't worry about useless things right now.

I should take advantage of the fact that he's not restoring, and simply think of how to send all of his arms flying.
annotated.instruct: Angry, growling snarl.

annotated.text: Grrr...
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Badigadi continued to groan, but a new arm didn’t come out.

And contrary to that, the arm that was restored before was now covered in some turtle like armor.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I wonder what it is.

In the next instant, from the remaining 4 arms, 2 vanished.

The arms and the gauntlets were sucked into the armor.

And the remaining two arms got thicker.

They got thicker with a gurgling sound.

The remaining two.

Now that they’re thicker, can an I cut them…?

No, I can. The harder the object, the better this sword cuts. There’s no meaning in it even if he reinforced his arms and increased his defense.

After promptly deciding that, I kicked the ground and closed in on the Fighting God.

An alarm bell rang somewhere in my mind.

But no matter what the enemy was planning, I had already revealed my trump card.

With every passing moment, my mana was approaching zero.

If I didn’t attack, I couldn’t win.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: AAAAAAaaaaa!
annotated.speaker: IMMORTAL DEMON LORD ATOFE
annotated.instruct: Agonized, high-pitched scream.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I could only shout.

In doing so, power came out.

Denying both fear and uncertainty, a small amount of courage showed its face.

This small amount of courage became profound.

Charging at him to obtain victory, just like Eris.

I rammed into the Fighting God.

He staggered, but took the blow.

I swung my right hand.

Biting into his left hand, I kept cutting.

I brought out my left hand,

And pushed the shotgun against where I cut,

And then shouted.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with intense urgency and rising power, building up to a climactic moment of courage.

annotated.text: SHOTGUN TRIGGER!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Short, sharp, and explosive, like the trigger being pulled with immense force.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Both Badigadi’s arm and the Fighting God armor went flying.

But at the same time, I was also sent flying.

I was knocked back.

Badigadi’s remaining arm.

I was hit by it.

The entire front of the Magic Armor was completely destroyed.

The shockwave traveled to the interior and my body was assaulted by a pressure that felt like it would crush me flat.

I fell on my back.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with dramatic impact, describing the aftermath of the shotgun blast with vivid, cinematic detail.

annotated.text: Ghaough.....ghaohu.....
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deep, guttural, and pained, reflecting the Fighting God's suffering and rage.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I coughed up blood.

My heart screamed ‘not yet!’ in vain.

I had misread him.

The reason Badigadi reduced his arms to two was for a single devastating attack.

Let your opponent cut your flesh so that you can cut him to the bone, was it?
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of realization and regret, highlighting the narrator's mistake and the enemy's cunning.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He drove his fist accurately into the crack, breaking the Magic Armor apart.

But not yet.

Not yet.

Just one more.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a sense of determination and urgency, emphasizing the narrator's refusal to give up.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I can’t move.

The movement of the Magic Armor is faltering.

The damage can’t be fixed.

Right underneath the main body(me), is what could be called the core of the Magic Armor.

If that was broken, the Magic Armor will begin to fail.

I won’t say that it couldn’t move. It wasn’t constructed that simply.

But it could only move.

In this battle, it’s fatally slow.

I began transmitting mana in a hurry.

Right, I still have mana left.

It could still move.

My mana hadn’t dried up yet.

I could still fight.

Then why couldn’t I move?
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of desperation and internal struggle, showing the narrator's physical and emotional limits.

annotated.text: Good plan, good fighting spirit......
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Deep, mocking, and triumphant, reflecting the Fighting God's confidence and disdain.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: Badigadi approached me as I couldn’t move.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of impending doom, describing the narrator's helplessness as the enemy closes in.

annotated.text: And a good match. Farewell Rudeus. Not even Laplace thought this elaborately.
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of finality and respect, acknowledging the battle's conclusion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Badigadi raised his fist above his head.

A fist like a cannon.

And it was thrown off─
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a sense of impending danger and urgency, describing the dramatic moment before the attack.

annotated.text: GAA!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Short, sharp, and panicked, reflecting the sudden realization of danger.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Something red flew in from under his arm and knocked the fist off course.

The arm was cut off at the base and flew in midair.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of shock and awe, describing the unexpected intervention and its consequences.

annotated.text: Mngh!
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Pained and desperate, reflecting Eris's struggle and the breaking of her sword.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
There were only a few things that had the color red in this forest.

It’s Eris.

Was she following us? Had she been right behind us?

I didn’t know.

There’s no other backup.

Only Eris jumped in.

But in the next instant, I realized something was out of place.

The sword.

Eris’s sword broke.

The famous
annotated.instruct: Proud and defiant, emphasizing the significance of the broken sword.

annotated.text: Elegant Phoenix Dragon Sword
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of disbelief and sorrow, highlighting the broken sword's importance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
broke at the base.

Of course, up until now, even when damage was taken on the surface, the base was never broken.

If it’s forcefully cut from the base, then it’ll obviously break.
annotated.instruct: Pained and furious, reflecting Eris's emotional and physical turmoil.

annotated.text: GAAAAAAaaaaa!
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of determination and sacrifice, highlighting the group's bravery despite the odds.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But Eris did not cease.

As if she hadn’t realized that her sword broke, while crying out, she continued to face the Fighting God.

Looking again, it’s not just her.

Coming out of the forest one after the other as if chasing Eris were Sylphy, Ruijerd, Ghyslaine, and Isolte.

But it’s too late.
annotated.instruct: Deep, mocking, and arrogant, reflecting the Fighting God's disdain for the group's efforts.

annotated.text: It’s foolish to stand before me alone!
annotated.speaker: FIGHTING GOD BADIGADI
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of urgency and resolve, describing the narrator's final act of heroism.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Badigadi approached Eris.

There was nothing to protect her.

In that instant, I activated the escape function and slipped out of the Magic Armor.

And from the back of the Magic Armor, I took out the single sword that I had stored there.

The second I grabbed the handle, a tremendous feeling of omnipotence ran through my body.

An overwhelming amount of mana.

Upon which I poured in even more mana.

With the intention of filling the sword with all of my remaining mana.

I didn’t think of using it myself.

But in front of me, there was a family member whose sword broke.

Who, in order to protect me, was brandishing a broken sword.

I threw the sword with her as the target.
annotated.instruct: Short, urgent, and emotional, reflecting the narrator's concern for Eris.

annotated.text: Eris!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of awe and revelation, describing the arrival of the powerful cursed sword.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
In a loose arc, the cursed sword flew.

Eris turned around and grabbed it.

Dragon King Sword Kajakuto.

The world’s strongest and most famous cursed sword. The peak of the cursed swords forged by the blacksmith master Yulian.

Eris held it above her head.
annotated.instruct: Pained and determined, reflecting Eris's resolve as she prepares for the final battle.

annotated.text: GAAAAAAAHH!
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Pained and furious, reflecting Eris's final, desperate cry as the battle reaches its climax.

annotated.text: GH, That’s.....!
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Start with a sharp gasp, showing surprise and shock.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: A downwards swing.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a calm, detached tone, describing the aftermath of the attack.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Right before impact, just for an instant, the Fighting God’s body floated.

The sword bit right into the Fighting God’s body.

And at the same time, a bright flash filled my vision.

The explosion numbed my eardrums.

Something overwhelming dominated the place.

Destruction unfolded before me.

But there was no blast.

Nor a shockwave.

Only silence came.

The destruction headed towards the interior.

The mana driven into the sword became a sphere and enveloped Badigadi.

It wasn’t just Eris’s power.

The mana I had loaded it with was being released by the cursed sword.

And inside the sphere of magic...

I saw it.

While slowly rising up to the surface, its interior contents were being destroyed.

The Fighting God Armor was cracking and breaking.

Badigadi, without a sound, was being compressed and disappearing.

I thought that Badigadi would struggle.

But he couldn’t do anything.

The Fighting God Armor stopped functioning, and Badigadi was being destroyed as soon as he regenerated.

...............

The sphere disappeared.

The fragments of the armor left in mid-air fell towards the Earth Dragon Valley.

While making cling and clang noises, the fragments rolled down into the valley.

With the Dragon King sword stuck in it.

In just the armor.

Badigadi’s black body had disappeared without a trace.

I gazed at it.

I gazed at it for a while.

Until the sound was lost in the valley and the armor disappeared.

Close by, Badigadi’s arm still remained.

It wasn’t moving.

It wasn’t even twitching.

There was no sign of restoration.

Was he dead?

Did we win?

Is there still something else?

Is it soon?

Something’s not going to rise up and appear with a FUHAHAHA is it?

With those feelings, I simply stared at the valley.

Nothing rose up.

There’s no sign of anything rising up.

Only stillness was left in that place.

I heard someone falling from behind.

When I turned around, Eris was on her knees.

With a ghastly pale face.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a slow, dramatic pace, emphasizing the intensity and scale of the destruction.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I rushed over in a hurry.

An injury?

Was she countered?

I immediately stretched out my hand to cast healing magic, but I also fell to my knees.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with urgency and concern, showing the speaker's worry for Eris.

annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Mutter weakly, showing exhaustion and pain.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
It’s not an injury.

What I’m feeling, and the look on Eris’s face, I recognized them.

Mana exhaustion.

The Dragon King Sword Kajakuto had sucked up all of my mana and exhausted Eris’s as well.

This was probably the first time since childhood that Eris’s magic had been this exhausted.

While blinking in surprise, she sat down.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a steady, informative tone, explaining the cause of Eris's condition.

annotated.text: Eris.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Call out Eris's name with concern and urgency.

annotated.text: Rudeus.....your hair has gotten whiter again.
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Speak with a mix of worry and realization, noting the change in appearance.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
She said so and touched my head.

I don’t know about myself.

But some portion of Eris’s hair had also become white.

Her hair now had white streaks.
annotated.instruct: Respond with a calm, observational tone, acknowledging the shared change.

annotated.text: Yours is too.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Say with a mix of acceptance and dry humor, acknowledging the shared change.

annotated.text: Really......then we match.
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a heavy, emotional tone, showing Eris's complete exhaustion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Eris said that and fell forward.

She didn’t lose consciousness.

She had simply used up all of her power.

I wanted to fall down on top of her, but I held on.
annotated.instruct: Call out Rudy's name with worry and urgency.

annotated.text: Rudy!
annotated.speaker: SYLPHY
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a concerned tone, describing the group's reaction to the situation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Sylphy looked worried when she saw our faces.

Not just Sylphy.

Ruijerd, Ghislaine, and Isolte.......
annotated.instruct: Ask urgently, showing concern for Cliff's whereabouts.

annotated.text: Sylphy, where’s Cliff!?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Explain with a hesitant, apologetic tone, detailing the events that transpired.

annotated.text: Umm, after healing the wounds of others, he was carried by Zanoba and Doga to the village. We immediately chased after you, but thought that we'd be a bother, so we hesitated....but then Eris jumped in alone......huh?
annotated.speaker: SYLPHY
annotated.instruct: Narrate with confusion and concern, showing the group's reaction to Eris's condition.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
When Sylphy felt Eris’s head, she tilted her head in confusion.

She probably immediately used healing magic.

But Eris wasn’t injured.

She wasn’t going to get up anytime soon.
annotated.instruct: Explain with a calm, informative tone, clarifying the cause of Eris's exhaustion.

annotated.text: It’s magic exhaustion. That sword sucks out all of the wielder’s mana.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Respond with a quiet, understanding tone, acknowledging the explanation.

annotated.text: …Ah, so that’s how it is.
annotated.speaker: SYLPHY
annotated.instruct: Give instructions with a firm, determined tone, showing urgency and responsibility.

annotated.text: For now, Sylphy, can you put the arm fallen over there in one of the undamaged magic circles? After that, I want you to take Eris, return to the village, and report to Orsted about the current details and bring Cliff back with you.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a weary, reflective tone, assessing the current situation and future challenges.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I stood up.

The MK. Zero was destroyed.

I myself was basically entirely out of mana.....but I could still move.

We don’t how much time lag there is before Badigadi revives.

At the very least, with that much compressed magic, it looked like he was obliterated.

There’s no sign that the arm will regenerate.

I’d like to think that we have a lot of time.

However, wishful thinking like that may be presumptuous.

But the MK. Zero was destroyed. The MK. I was no more. In addition to my almost exhausted mana, in this situation where the barrier magic couldn’t be activated without Cliff, we couldn’t have Badigadi reviving from the bottom of the valley.

If we descend to the bottom of the valley and he’s waiting for us, victory would be far off.

There’d be no option but for Orsted to take the front line.

I wanted him to not use magic until the very end, but we may not have a choice.

I lacked the ability.

But I’d like to wait until we’re driven into an absolute corner.

I did all that I could.

It’s unknown whether or not Badigadi was moving at the bottom of the valley, but we should have restrained him at the very least.
annotated.instruct: Give instructions with a calm, authoritative tone, directing the group's next actions.

annotated.text: Ruijerd, Ghyslaine, and Isolte too, please follow me.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Ask with concern and curiosity, showing interest in Rudy's next move.

annotated.text: What will you do? Rudy.
annotated.speaker: ERIS
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a resolute, determined tone, showing the speaker's resolve despite exhaustion.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I’d done all I could.

But there was still something that I must do.

With my almost exhausted mana, there was something that I must do.
annotated.instruct: Declare with urgency and determination, showing a clear intent to act.

annotated.text: I’m going after Gisu!
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Urgent, determined tone with rising pitch.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Part 3

We immediately found Gisu.

Very easily and quickly.

I didn’t even have to use my almost exhausted mana. We found him that easily.

The moment we crossed the valley and entered the burnt-black forest.

Within the shadow of a big burnt tree.

Gisu had fallen there.

He had large burns all over and he was lying there with his body completely black.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: THE
annotated.text: Flashover
annotated.instruct: Mysterious, echoing tone with a slight pause.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I casted over the forest seemed to have burnt him as well.

He looked pretty dead to us when we first found him.

He didn’t move a muscle and looked like a black stone.

But the one who found him was Ruijerd, using his third eye.

It wasn’t a corpse.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: Gisu
annotated.instruct: Weak, barely audible whisper.

annotated.text: Yo, Senpai.
annotated.speaker: Gisu
annotated.instruct: Casual, slightly mocking tone with a smirk.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He hadn’t become a corpse yet, but it was clear that he was at death’s door.

I didn’t feel like curing him either.

This was why I came here.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text: But I didn’t feel like finishing him off right away either.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Hehee, Water Magic, Earth Magic, Demon Eyes, and Magic Armor.......I had countermeasures for each one of ‘em and yet look at me now.
annotated.speaker: Gisu
annotated.instruct: Defeated, sarcastic tone with a hint of bitterness.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Gisu was wearing many things.

A blue vest, a light brown chest protector, and something like a chain-mail.

Each of them was burnt now, but they were probably countermeasures for each type of magic.

This meant that him being able to withstand the Thunderfall in the Third City was not because of the Fighting God Armor’s power.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Now that you’ve come here, this means.....that even the final plan has ended in failure......
annotated.speaker: Gisu
annotated.instruct: Broken, strained voice with pauses.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Gisu was straining his now burnt cheeks.

The final plan.

Would it be okay to say that sending Badigadi out alone was a plan?
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Sword God, North God, Ogre God, Dark King.....if any one of ‘em were still left, it would’ve been different.......if they had listened to me that is.....

Part 4

Gisu was defeated.

That notion should be good enough, but my heart was still unclear.

I knew that I had gotten a shock.

Someone that you know dying in front of you like that is something incomprehensible.

He was an enemy. I was aware that he must be defeated.

But it’s not like I hated Gisu from the bottom of my heart.

Although, if we had lost in this battle and Eris or someone close to me had died, then it was possible that I would harbor hate.

If things had turned out that way, would my heart feel refreshed then?

Thinking that I would have been paid back by defeating the one who I hated the most.

I don’t know.

The only thing I could say was that the reason I was able to think like this while being exhausted was because I didn’t lose any of my loved ones during this battle.

I met the conditions for victory.

While preserving Orsted’s mana capacity, I was able to finish off every apostle.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a tone of mixed emotions, reflecting on the battle's outcome and Gisu's legacy.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
We had hard battles and there were failures as well, but it was a complete victory, that was unusual for me.

It’s possible that I've embarrassed myself by letting Gisu die like that.

Perhaps I could’ve brought Gisu to my side. I had taken that matter into consideration somewhere deep within my heart.

Even if I say this now, it’s something that can’t be helped.

Well, I’ll make sure to at least carry his bones to the graveyard.

I guess it’s fine if I put him next to Paul.

I thought about doing that as I burnt Gisu’s body.

Anyway, now it’s finally over.

I’m tired.

I only had a scarce amount of mana left.

My stamina was completely drained as well.

I’d lose consciousness the moment I hit the bed.

Though I couldn’t just sleep before completely sealing Badigadi......

But I want to return back to Sharia as fast as possible.

I want to sleep tight on my bed.

When I wake up, I’ll eat.

I’ll eat rice.

Oh right, this country had soy sauce.

I can eat a perfect egg-rice mix.

I’ll eat it when I get back.

I’ll eat to my heart’s content.

After that, it’s sexy time.

The abstinent Rudeus had died along with Gisu.

Sylphy, Roxy, or Eris......who should I choose?

How about all three of them together?

Eris might dislike it, but, it should be fine to try it out just once, right?

It’s my long-awaited moment.

Yep, long-awaited.

Let’s postpone the review for this battle.

I’ll try to forget what Gisu said this time.

Anyway, I’ll take a day-off.

I’m tired.

Behind him, towards the valley.

Hand.

It’s a hand.

Something was climbing out of the valley.

Something?

No, giving it a vague description like ‘something’ would be a grave mistake.

That hand.

The color of the hand was gold.

It was a golden gauntlet.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.text: Are you serious?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

Badigadi.

This is too fast.

So it’s possible that the remaining parts gathered together and regenerated in a short amount of time.

But its shape was different.

It had 2 arms, similar to when we brought it down, but its overall design had changed.

Its helmet was different and it wasn’t that tall either.

It wasn’t even 2 metres.

On top of that, it was holding a sword.

A large sword.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
The world’s strongest sword made by the King Dragon King himself.

Wrong.

This one was different.

This guy wasn’t Badigadi.

Even though he didn’t even twitch at that time.

He was still alive?

Come to think of it, he’s from the lineage of the Immortal Demon clan.

No, that’s wrong.

It’s that.

It’s the

Gisu was talking about.

So this is it.

Did he intend to do this from the start?

Or did he change it mid-way?

I thought it was strange.

I thought that it was strange that the Fighting God Armor wasn’t restoring itself.

It was intentionally not restoring itself.

And then, Alek wore the Fighting God Armor at the bottom of the valley and it was restored.

It was possible that they were making preliminary arrangements during the time Gisu was playing dead.

Something like dropping a part of Badigadi and the Fighting God Armor down the valley, resurrecting Alek……

Damnit.

Must we do it again?

Must we fight again?

We’re bored already.

Shouldn’t it be fine to just end it at that?

Cut it out already! Why did someone who already died come out now of all times!?

No, it’s my fault.

I didn’t properly dispose of Alek’s body.

I left it as is, thinking that I had defeated him, that I had won.

It might be different if I had burnt his body, but I left it as is.

But, just how was he still fine? Within those conditions. Beyond that state.

Well......it’s fine.

The past is in the past.

What to do now?

I don’t even have the MK. Zero now.

No allies.

Ghyslaine, Ruijerd, and Isolte.

And I, with almost completely exhausted mana.

With no weapons and no shield.

No method.

I don’t think we can win.

What should be done?

What to do? Could we win against North God Kalman the Third wearing the Fighting God Armor?

Could we at least shave off some of his power?

As if to say that he had been looking forward to this as a matter of course.

Just why were Aisha and Rudo Mercenary Group here?

Just why was there no one except Orsted when Alek arrived at the village?

Explaining that is a must.

Although I said that an explanation was needed, I’ll only finish it up with a few words.

It was Aisha’s deed.

It was Aisha’s work.

When the Teleport Formation and Communication Lithograph stopped working –

Aisha and Rudo Mercenary Group too were in the polar regions of confusion.

In a faraway land with their means of contact and movement sealed, anxiety and impatience were born.

Within those circumstances, Aisha was calm.

She calmly took things into consideration and thought.

If the fight had already started at the actual spot, then for them who were near the national border, it would be too late once they actually reached their destination, and the things that could be done were few as well.

The conclusion Aisha had arrived at took into consideration the possibility of Gisu escaping while trying to re-store the Teleport Formation.

That is to say, the restoration of infrastructure.

Although, in addition to the Teleport Formations, the reserved formation that Aisha had took with her which corresponded with the formation at the office were all already destroyed.

There was no way.

Or so I would think, and give up.

Because I already gave up.

Her gifted brain recalled the secret arts of a certain person.

Those secret arts, which had a complete grasp of the damaged teleport formations of the other side and the formations that corresponded to those ones, were a technique capable of drawing such formations and able to teleport wherever desired.

Just who was that certain person?

That’s right, it was
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text: The Armored Dragon King
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text:
Perugius Dola.

She searched for a Stone Monument of the Seven Great World Powers near the national border in order to ask him for a favor.

Depending on whether she could find it, she would then travel to the Sky Fortress after using Perugius’s flute.

Perugius, who knew that we were helping a Demon Race, was reluctant.

He declared
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text: I’ll only make one.

annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

towards Aisha’s request, to which Aisha chose the option of creating a mag-ic formation at the national border which connected to the Supard Village.

And that’s how it was.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text: You were able to persuade Perugius, eh?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
After that, when I was in the middle of battle, everyone teleported from the Supard village.

They quickly made use of the teleport formation after hearing about the circumstances, and the inhabitants and the rest all took shelter at a city near the national border....or so how it went.

If we had prioritized on making a normal teleport formation rather than making one for Roxy’s return to Sha-ria to summon the Magic Armor
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text: MK. Zero
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
, it would have been almost in vain.....

It was somehow clever that Roxy’s mistake was followed up by Aisha.

Although it was inevitable that Roxy felt pretty guilty after that and curled herself up.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text: Around here?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text: Yeah, clean it aaallll up. It should be fine to spread the area a little more, right?
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text: I guess, got it.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text: When you’re done, call me again. I’ll make the Mercenary group carry the wood and all.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text: Roger.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
And so, it had been a month since the fight.

Although we were prepared while staying vigilant, there was no sign of any more battles.

It seemed that there would no longer be any battles.

Therefore, I asked Sylphy, Roxy, and Zanoba to return back to Sharia. I also asked Eris to return back under the pretext of making her their guard.

I asked of them this because the teleport formations used for the summoning of MK. Zero and the one used by refugees were destroyed during the battle of Orsted and Alek; it took the same pattern just like the time with Perugius.

I had asked them to rebuild the office, restore the teleport formations and communication lithographs, and such.

It seemed that nothing happened at Sharia.

The receptionist Little Elf-chan was fine too.

The only damage was that the weapons and armor, and the documents in which Orsted wrote every day were buried.

The refugees of the Supard race travelled from the national border to Second City Irel, and came back to the Supard village using the teleport formation which was re-connected.

Afterwards, they were officially welcomed by the Biheiril Kingdom.

It was affirmed that Biheiril Kingdom would be accepting the Supard Race as citizens.

They weren’t in any position to say no after losing both Ogre God and the third city.

They added a condition for accepting the Supards as official citizens, in that at least 3 people from the Supard Race should choose to do a profession for the sake of Country.

It was the same as what happened with the Ogre Race.

For now, the selection of those three had finished, and we’re currently starting reconstruction on the Supard village.

If the reconstruction continues without any incident, then the Supards would be able to live in the Biheiril Kingdom’s urban area.

We had defeated all of the apostles, and had made the Biheiril Kingdom, Ogre Race, and Supard Race our al-lies.

We were victorious.

But, did we really gain complete victory?
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.text: Rudeus-dono.
annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Short, abrupt tone, as if calling out to someone.

annotated.speaker: UNKNOWN
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause between questions and answers.

annotated.text:
While I pondered, the lumbering of woods continued. Unaware of my surroundings, Sándor was now stand-ing behind me.

It wasn’t just Sándor.

Ghyslaine, Isolte, and Doga were there too.

Sándor came back about 10 days later after the fight was over.

He was knocked off into the sea by the Fighting God and drifted ashore to Ogre Island, where he strained himself to recuperate.

Or should I say how admirable it was that he came back alive after fighting against the Fighting God?
annotated.instruct: Polite, slightly hesitant tone, as if requesting something.

annotated.text: Thank you for your efforts. What happened?

The work of Sándor and the rest was over.

They were at best Ariel’s subordinates.

If there was no fight, then they could only return back.

annotated.text: Sándor-san. Thank you very much. If it weren’t for you, then all of this wouldn’t have happened.

annotated.text: Of course. Please convey to Her Majesty that if something happens from now on, then Her Majesty can in-form me first. That I would be willing to cooperate.

annotated.instruct: Rudeus Greyrat speaks with a composed, diplomatic tone, expressing willingness to cooperate.

annotated.text: I understand.

annotated.instruct: Sandor replies with a simple, direct tone, showing understanding.

Sándor, Doga, Ghyslaine, and Isolte.

Each one of them was as strong as King class or above.

I couldn’t thank her enough for lending me such strong people.

After giving an elegant bow, she smiled.

The same as before, a beautiful woman.

I wonder just what the heck the males of the Asura Kingdom were thinking if she’s still unmarried.

annotated.text:
Sándor bowed once and turned on his heels.

But after seeing his back, I recalled something that I had completely forgotten and called out to him.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after the first sentence.

annotated.text: Um....it was regretful what happened to Atofe-sama.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Hesitant and apologetic tone, speaking with uncertainty.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Sándor came back.

But it was only him who returned.

Atofe was still missing.

If she was washed away by the sea then she wouldn’t be found for another several years.

It was the same with Moore too.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a somber undertone.

annotated.text: ......There’s no need to worry about Mother. I think if you give her enough time, she would suddenly make her appearance some day. I think the most regretful thing that had happened was Ogre God’s death.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Calm and reflective, with a touch of reassurance.

annotated.text: That’s.....right.
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Short and subdued, with a tone of agreement.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Ogre God’s death was confirmed.

He put up a good fight against Fighting God.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of solemnity.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
But he wasn’t one of the Immortal Demon Race. He used up all of his strength in the end and died.

Even though I had finally reconciled with him too...
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of resignation.

annotated.text: Although nothing can be gained by just mourning the dead.
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Calm and resolute, with a firm emphasis on moving forward.

annotated.text: Indeed. We must look ahead of ourselves.
annotated.speaker: SANDOR
annotated.instruct: Calm and determined, with a tone of solemn commitment.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I had promised Malta.

That if he were to die then I would be protecting the survivors of the Ogre Race.

Right now, there was no one who would be a threat to Ogre Race, but if something happened then I’d want to protect them even if there wasn’t a promise.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of reflection.

annotated.text: Well then, goodbye.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Polite and appreciative, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Yes. Many thanks for your hard work.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Polite and sincere, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Ah, right.....Please take care of Alek.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Hesitant and sincere, with a soft tone.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of quiet observation.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Sándor said that and left.

And then Cliff could be seen coming my way as if replacing them.

Along with Elinalize.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of quiet observation.

annotated.text: Are they returning as well?

annotated.instruct: Respectful and polite, with a warm tone.

annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Respectful and polite, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Yeah. The relocation is over......in the end, I just couldn’t find out the cause of Plague, but it’s been almost a month now and the people living there have moved away......so I’ve decided to head back for now.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of reflection.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I was indebted to Cliff as well.

If it weren’t for him, the plague couldn’t have been cured.

It’s possible that the plague was the Dark King’s doing.
annotated.instruct: Grateful and sincere, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Cliff-senpai. Thank you very much. If you hadn’t come, then just what would've happened......
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Calm and reassuring, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Well, I do think that you would’ve been able to something, since it’s you. If the plague relapses, contact me.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Grateful and sincere, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Yes.......I’ve been getting nothing but favors from you; just how should I show my gratitude, I wonder?
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Calm and sincere, with a tone of mutual respect.

annotated.text: The reason I’m able to work hard in Milis while leaving Lize and Clive is because your family is looking after mine. We are of equal status in that regard.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a tone of quiet gratitude.

annotated.text: I’m grateful if he says something like that.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight tone of gratitude.

annotated.text: Well then, till next time. I’ll be meeting your family on my way back, so are there any messages?

annotated.instruct: Direct and concise, with a calm and steady tone.

annotated.text: Got it.

annotated.instruct: Simple and straightforward, with a casual and brief delivery.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Cliff said that and left.

In the end, Elinalize winked at me. I’ve troubled her a lot as well, but didn’t say anything to her...... Well, I’d do that the next time we talk as neighbors.

But, I sure was saved by various people this time.

First was Cliff. If it weren’t for him, then the Supard race might have perished by the plague.

Then Sándor and Doga. If it weren’t for them, I wouldn’t be standing here right now.

Atofe’s timing looked like God’s itself.

The Atofe-hand and the attack at Ogre Island at just the right time.

It could be said that this victory with almost no injuries was thanks to Atofe.

That Atofe was now missing, that is to say, I wanted to search for her in the sea once things had calmed down as a way of not showing too much ingratitude.

The battle was now over and everyone was returning.

A big event had ended, and it looked like we were breaking up as a result.

It was somehow lonely.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a reflective and contemplative tone.

annotated.text: Alright.
annotated.speaker: CLIFF GRIMOIRE
annotated.instruct: Simple and straightforward, with a casual and brief delivery.

As I pondered such things, the lumbering of the woods was finished.

In front of my eyes was a clean, stretched-out ground.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly proud undertone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR

The trees that were pulled out from their roots were neatly lined up using Earth Magic.

I had done a nice job if I say so myself.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly self-satisfied tone.

annotated.text: Now then, Aisha is......hm.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly hesitant and thoughtful tone.

annotated.text: Yes, I understand.

Norn turned on her heels and quickly ran towards the village.

Ruijerd who was left behind was now walking up to me.

annotated.text: Right.

annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slightly reflective and contemplative tone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR

Ruijerd was engaged in the reconstruction of the Supard village.

After that, he would probably come and go from our office, or be placed as the Biheiril Kingdom’s negotiator.

Norn was clinging to Ruijerd.

She too, until this village had finished rebuilding, intended to help Ruijerd.

annotated.text: After the village’s completion, please do visit our house in Sharia.

Ruijerd laughed and then eyed me.

His height hadn’t changed very much.

annotated.text: .....You became really strong, didn’t you? I never would have thought that you would become one of the Seven Great World Powers.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD

annotated.text: If it’s the you right now then even you can become one, Ruijerd-san. If it’s you, I would be done in by just one punch, in just one punch.

annotated.instruct: Confident and slightly boastful, with a playful undertone.

annotated.text: Don’t joke around.

Ruijerd looked at me a little, gave out a little laugh, removed the pendant hanging from his neck, and held it out towards me.

It was Roxy’s pendant.

annotated.text: I’ll return this back to you now.

The pendant I gave to Ruijerd when we first parted.

Roxy’s pendant.

Unaware, this pendant had become my mark.

The pendant which was my motive for setting out into the world.
annotated.instruct: Reflective and emotional, with a slow and deliberate pace.

annotated.text: I understand.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Calm and sincere, with a slightly emotional undertone.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
I accepted that pendant.

Before, when I handed him this pendant, it was over a trivial matter.

When we parted, I never intended for him to give it back to me. I hoped that he would hold onto it.

Or perhaps I wanted to have a link with him.

But he had returned it now.

Because we were already brethren.

Because we won’t be parting for quite some time now.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after the first sentence.

annotated.text: Ruijerd-san, Please take care of me from now on.
annotated.speaker: RUDEUS GREYRAT
annotated.instruct: Humble and slightly self-deprecating, with a warm tone.

annotated.text: Yeah. Though I might lack the ability.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD
annotated.instruct: Confident and reassuring, with a calm and steady delivery.

annotated.text: We’ll just have to compensate for each other’s mistakes.

annotated.text: Pfft, that’s right.
annotated.speaker: RUIJERD

I laughed and Ruijerd too smiled.

Part 2

Norn came back along with Mercenary Group and left with Ruijerd.

I left the place as well and started walking towards the Teleport Formation.

I thought of finally returning back to Sharia.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a sudden, sharp emphasis.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
Then I realized that someone was approaching me from behind.

It was Orsted.

Just as always with the black helmet.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slight pause after the first sentence.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
He wasn’t alone.

Behind him was a black-haired boy who was following like a loyal retainer.

It was Aleksander Ryback.
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration with a slow and deliberate pace.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.instruct: Neutral, even narration.

annotated.speaker: NARRATOR
annotated.text:
From that day forward, he started following Orsted everywhere as his subordinate.

Like Moore, who followed Atofe.

Like Sylvaril, who followed Perugius.

As if to say that he had been in this position since hundreds of years ago.

I wanted to make him acknowledge me as his superior, but if we were to fight, I’d lose, so I kept quiet.

However, no matter how many times I see him, I end up getting cautious.
annotated.instruct: Reflective and slightly tense, with a calm and measured delivery.

That evening, Orsted and I proceeded towards the Earth Dragon Valley.

Towards the bottom of the Earth Dragon Valley.

A leveled path where blue mushrooms and moss were growing in abundance.

There was a carefully hidden small hole on the wall.

The hole that was about 1 metre in diameter was in a slightly curved position. It looked like a dead end at a glance if seen from outside.

However, a huge room awaited if someone were to proceed some 10 metres inside it.

There, a large magic formation was shedding light with one sword as its core.

Though I say it’s large, its radius was 5 metres at best.

One male was lying within that formation.

It was Demon Lord Badigadi.

His body had been separated into 5 pieces, and each of them were sealed in different places in the valley.

His main body was here.

This barrier would never get destroyed unless all of the remaining 4 seals were destroyed first.

And then, the barrier was operating using the mana of Badigadi’s body, which was further amplified with the Dragon King Sword and Fighting God Armor as a catalyst.

It could keep operating almost forever.

The Barrier Magic Formation was reverently made by Perugius himself.

It was the God-Class barrier magic created in order to seal the Demon God.

If the sealing object that would become the medium and the magic item that would become the intermedi-ary were strong enough, they could increase the barrier’s strength.

In addition to the Fighting God Armor, even the Dragon King Sword was used by this seal as a catalyst. It was powerful enough that not even Orsted could break out of it.

It’s possible that using two God-Class equipment as one part of the barrier was somewhat wasteful.

However, both of them would be terrifying weapons in the hands of the enemy.

Since the enemy proved this by using the teleport formations for their own gain, if these things were getting used up here then it’s not such a bad thing.
annotated.instruct: Narrate with a solemn, informative tone, explaining complex details and implications.

If this was destroyed then there would be no choice left but to give up.

That’s the conclusion I’d come with.

Orsted had requested Perugius to set up this barrier.

He bowed his head and requested to borrow his strength.

And, Perugius acknowledged that.

He became Orsted’s brethren, his ally.

But Perugius was someone that must be killed.

Which meant that Orsted had chosen the path of betrayal.

I owed both Orsted and Perugius a lot.

As an individual, it’s a complex feeling.

But I could understand that Orsted had no choice left but to choose that path.

On top of that, if it’s something that Orsted had decided on, then I was in no position to complain.

I did think that it would’ve been nice if we at least knew some way to reach Hitogami’s place without using the five Dragon Race treasures, but it was clear that just a little bit of research wasn’t going to be enough to find it.

The enemy was in front of me right now.
